# Page: Input File Format

# Input File Format

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [app/packmol.f90](app/packmol.f90)
- [src/checkpoint.f90](src/checkpoint.f90)
- [src/cli_parser.f90](src/cli_parser.f90)
- [src/getinp.f90](src/getinp.f90)
- [src/input.f90](src/input.f90)
- [src/output.f90](src/output.f90)
- [src/setsizes.f90](src/setsizes.f90)
- [testing/input_files/solvprotein.inp](testing/input_files/solvprotein.inp)
- [testing/structure_files/protein.pdb](testing/structure_files/protein.pdb)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page provides a complete specification of Packmol's input file format (`.inp` files). The input file controls all aspects of molecular packing: which molecules to pack, how many copies, where to place them, and optimization parameters. The format is parsed by [src/setsizes.f90]() and [src/getinp.f90]().

For information about command-line execution modes, see [Command-Line Interface](#3.5). For details about specific geometric constraints, see [Spatial Constraints](#3.2). For periodic boundary conditions, see [Periodic Boundary Conditions](#3.3).

---

## Input File Structure Overview

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    INPUT["Input File (.inp)"] --> GLOBAL["Global Keywords"]
    INPUT --> STRUCTURES["Structure Blocks"]
    
    GLOBAL --> REQUIRED["Required Global Keywords"]
    GLOBAL --> OPTIONAL["Optional Global Keywords"]
    
    REQUIRED --> TOL["tolerance"]
    REQUIRED --> OUT["output"]
    REQUIRED --> FTYPE["filetype (default: pdb)"]
    
    OPTIONAL --> SEED["seed"]
    OPTIONAL --> OPTI["Optimization Parameters"]
    OPTIONAL --> PBC["pbc"]
    OPTIONAL --> ADVO["Advanced Options"]
    
    STRUCTURES --> STRUC1["structure [filename]"]
    STRUCTURES --> STRUC2["structure [filename]"]
    STRUCTURES --> STRUCN["structure [filename]"]
    
    STRUC1 --> NUM1["number"]
    STRUC1 --> CONS1["Constraints"]
    STRUC1 --> OPTS1["Structure Options"]
    STRUC1 --> END1["end structure"]
    
    CONS1 --> INSIDE["inside cube/box/sphere/etc"]
    CONS1 --> OUTSIDE["outside cube/box/sphere/etc"]
    CONS1 --> OVER["over/above/below plane"]
    CONS1 --> FIXED["fixed x y z beta gama teta"]
    
    OPTS1 --> RADIUS["radius"]
    OPTS1 --> ATOMS["atoms...end atoms blocks"]
    OPTS1 --> CHAINS["resnumbers/changechains/chain"]
    OPTS1 --> RESTART["restart_from/restart_to"]
```

**Diagram: Overall Input File Structure**

The input file consists of global keywords followed by one or more `structure...end structure` blocks. Each structure block specifies a molecule type, how many copies to pack, and where to place them.

Sources: [src/getinp.f90:62-935](), [src/setsizes.f90:143-287](), [testing/input_files/solvprotein.inp:1-35]()

---

## Required Global Keywords

These keywords must appear in every input file (outside structure blocks):

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `tolerance` | `<distance>` | Minimum distance between atoms (Å). Sets the packing tolerance. | [src/getinp.f90:543-556]() |
| `output` | `<filename>` | Output file path. Extension determines format if `filetype` not specified. | [src/getinp.f90:259-272]() |
| `filetype` | `pdb`\|`tinker`\|`xyz` | Coordinate file format. Default: `pdb` | [src/setsizes.f90:143-168]() |

**Example:**
```
tolerance 2.0
output mixture.pdb
filetype pdb
```

Sources: [src/getinp.f90:259-272](), [src/getinp.f90:538-556](), [src/setsizes.f90:143-168]()

---

## Optional Global Keywords

### Random Seed and Initial Point

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `seed` | `<integer>`\|`-1` | Random seed for initial point generation. Use `-1` for time-based seed. | [src/getinp.f90:68-71]() |
| `randominitialpoint` | (none) | Start with random positions instead of constraint-satisfying positions. | [src/getinp.f90:72-73]() |

### Optimization Parameters

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `nloop` | `<integer>` | Maximum GENCAN iterations for full optimization. Default: `200*ntype` | [src/getinp.f90:104-113]() |
| `nloop0` | `<integer>` | Maximum GENCAN iterations for initial constraint satisfaction. Default: `20*ntype` | [src/getinp.f90:109-113]() |
| `maxit` | `<integer>` | Maximum iterations per GENCAN call. Default: `20` | [src/getinp.f90:100-103]() |
| `precision` | `<real>` | Convergence precision for optimization. Default: `0.01` | [src/getinp.f90:78-81]() |
| `discale` | `<real>` | Initial tolerance scale factor. Default: `1.1` | [src/getinp.f90:114-117]() |
| `movefrac` | `<real>` | Fraction of molecules to move in `movebad` heuristic. Default: `0.05` | [src/getinp.f90:82-85]() |
| `movebadrandom` | (none) | Move bad molecules randomly instead of to constraint centroids. | [src/getinp.f90:86-88]() |
| `disable_movebad` | (none) | Disable the `movebad` heuristic entirely. | [src/getinp.f90:89-91]() |

### Short-Range Penalty System

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `use_short_tol` | (none) | Enable short-range penalty for all atoms. | [src/getinp.f90:143-145]() |
| `short_tol_dist` | `<distance>` | Distance threshold for short-range penalty. Default: `tolerance/2` | [src/getinp.f90:741-759]() |
| `short_tol_scale` | `<real>` | Scale factor for short-range penalty. Default: `3.0` | [src/getinp.f90:761-776]() |

### Periodic Boundary Conditions

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `pbc` | `<xlen> <ylen> <zlen>` | Define cubic PBC box with side lengths. | [src/getinp.f90:167-198]() |
| `pbc` | `<xmin> <ymin> <zmin> <xmax> <ymax> <zmax>` | Define rectangular PBC box with min/max coordinates. | [src/getinp.f90:167-198]() |

See [Periodic Boundary Conditions](#3.3) for detailed documentation.

### Output Control

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `writeout` | `<integer>` | Frequency of output file writes during optimization. Default: `10` | [src/getinp.f90:94-97]() |
| `writebad` | (none) | Write intermediate files when molecules violate constraints. | [src/getinp.f90:76-77]() |
| `writecrd` | `<filename>` | Also write output in CHARMM CRD format. | [src/getinp.f90:146-149]() |
| `add_amber_ter` | (none) | Add `TER` records between molecules in PDB output. | [src/getinp.f90:126-128]() |
| `amber_ter_preserve` | (none) | Preserve `TER` records from fixed molecule input files. | [src/getinp.f90:129-131]() |
| `add_box_sides` | `[<padding>]` | Add `CRYST1` record to PDB output with box dimensions. | [src/getinp.f90:150-158]() |
| `hexadecimal_indices` | (none) | Use hexadecimal for atom/residue indices if they exceed decimal limits. | [src/getinp.f90:98-99]() |

### System Control

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `sidemax` | `<distance>` | Maximum system dimension for spatial grid setup. Default: `1000.0` | [src/getinp.f90:118-121]() |
| `fbins` | `<real>` | Linked-cell bin parameter for spatial partitioning. Default: `sqrt(3)` | [src/getinp.f90:122-125]() |
| `avoid_overlap` | `yes`\|`no` | Whether to avoid overlap with fixed molecules at initial point. Default: `yes` | [src/getinp.f90:132-139]() |
| `packall` | (none) | Pack all molecule types simultaneously instead of sequentially. | [src/getinp.f90:140-142]() |

### Debugging

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `check` | (none) | Check gradient computation (for debugging). | [src/getinp.f90:74-75]() |
| `chkgrad` | (none) | Detailed gradient checking. | [src/getinp.f90:92-93]() |
| `iprint1` | `<integer>` | GENCAN verbosity level 1. Default: `2` | [src/getinp.f90:159-162]() |
| `iprint2` | `<integer>` | GENCAN verbosity level 2. Default: `2` | [src/getinp.f90:163-166]() |

Sources: [src/getinp.f90:62-249]()

## Structure Block Format

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START["structure filename.pdb"] --> NUMBER["number N"]
    NUMBER --> CONSTRAINTS["Constraint Definitions"]
    CONSTRAINTS --> ATOMS_BLOCK["atoms...end atoms blocks (optional)"]
    ATOMS_BLOCK --> OPTIONS["Structure-Specific Options"]
    OPTIONS --> END["end structure"]
    
    CONSTRAINTS --> INS["inside cube/box/sphere/ellipsoid/cylinder"]
    CONSTRAINTS --> OUT["outside cube/box/sphere/ellipsoid/cylinder"]
    CONSTRAINTS --> PLANE["over/above/below plane/xygauss"]
    CONSTRAINTS --> FIX["fixed x y z beta gama teta"]
    
    ATOMS_BLOCK --> AT_START["atoms i j k ..."]
    AT_START --> AT_CONS["Atom-specific constraints"]
    AT_START --> AT_RAD["Atom-specific radius/fscale"]
    AT_START --> AT_END["end atoms"]
    
    OPTIONS --> RESTARTS["restart_from/restart_to"]
    OPTIONS --> PDB_OPTS["PDB: resnumbers/changechains/chain/segid"]
    OPTIONS --> NLOOP_OPT["nloop/nloop0 (override global)"]
    OPTIONS --> MAXMOVE["maxmove"]
    OPTIONS --> CONSTRAIN_ROT["constrain_rotation x/y/z min max"]
    OPTIONS --> CENTER["center/centerofmass"]
```

**Diagram: Structure Block Components**

Each `structure...end structure` block defines one molecule type to pack.

Sources: [src/getinp.f90:274-494](), [src/getinp.f90:789-807]()

### Structure Block Keywords

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Context | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|---------|----------------|
| `structure` | `<filename>` | Begin structure block. Filename contains molecular coordinates. | Block start | [src/getinp.f90:278-281]() |
| `end structure` | (none) | End structure block. | Block end | [src/getinp.f90:65-66]() |
| `number` | `<integer>` | Number of copies of this molecule to pack. Required. | Inside block | [src/setsizes.f90:243-253]() |

**Example:**
```
structure water.pdb
  number 1000
  inside box 0. 0. 0. 40. 40. 40.
end structure
```

Sources: [src/getinp.f90:278-281](), [src/setsizes.f90:196-253]()

---

## Geometric Constraints

```mermaid
graph TD
    CONSTRAINT["Geometric Constraint"] --> SCOPE["Constraint Scope"]
    CONSTRAINT --> TYPE["Constraint Type"]
    
    SCOPE --> ALL["All atoms of molecule"]
    SCOPE --> SPECIFIC["Specific atoms only"]
    
    SPECIFIC --> ATOMS_SYNTAX["atoms i j k ...<br/>constraint<br/>end atoms"]
    
    TYPE --> INSIDE["inside"]
    TYPE --> OUTSIDE["outside"]
    TYPE --> PLANE["over/above/below"]
    TYPE --> FIXED["fixed"]
    
    INSIDE --> IN_CUBE["cube x y z side"]
    INSIDE --> IN_BOX["box xmin ymin zmin xmax ymax zmax"]
    INSIDE --> IN_SPHERE["sphere x y z radius"]
    INSIDE --> IN_ELLIPSOID["ellipsoid x y z a b c"]
    INSIDE --> IN_CYLINDER["cylinder x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2 radius length"]
    
    OUTSIDE --> OUT_CUBE["cube x y z side"]
    OUTSIDE --> OUT_BOX["box xmin ymin zmin xmax ymax zmax"]
    OUTSIDE --> OUT_SPHERE["sphere x y z radius"]
    OUTSIDE --> OUT_ELLIPSOID["ellipsoid x y z a b c"]
    OUTSIDE --> OUT_CYLINDER["cylinder x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2 radius length"]
    
    PLANE --> PLANE_ABOVE["plane a b c d (above)"]
    PLANE --> PLANE_BELOW["plane a b c d (below)"]
    PLANE --> GAUSS_ABOVE["xygauss a b c d sigmax sigmay (above)"]
    PLANE --> GAUSS_BELOW["xygauss a b c d sigmax sigmay (below)"]
```

**Diagram: Constraint Type Hierarchy**

Sources: [src/getinp.f90:564-737]()

### Constraint Type Reference

| Constraint | Code Type | Syntax | Parameters | Line Reference |
|------------|-----------|--------|------------|----------------|
| Fixed position | `ityperest=1` | `fixed x y z beta gama teta` | Center position + Euler angles (degrees) | [src/getinp.f90:564-574]() |
| Inside cube | `ityperest=2` | `inside cube x y z side` | Cube center + side length | [src/getinp.f90:579-584]() |
| Inside box | `ityperest=3` | `inside box xmin ymin zmin xmax ymax zmax` | Box corners | [src/getinp.f90:585-592]() |
| Inside sphere | `ityperest=4` | `inside sphere x y z radius` | Sphere center + radius | [src/getinp.f90:593-598]() |
| Inside ellipsoid | `ityperest=5` | `inside ellipsoid x y z a b c` | Ellipsoid center + semi-axes | [src/getinp.f90:599-607]() |
| Inside cylinder | `ityperest=12` | `inside cylinder x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2 radius length` | Endpoints + radius + length | [src/getinp.f90:608-631]() |
| Outside cube | `ityperest=6` | `outside cube x y z side` | Cube center + side length | [src/getinp.f90:639-644]() |
| Outside box | `ityperest=7` | `outside box xmin ymin zmin xmax ymax zmax` | Box corners | [src/getinp.f90:645-652]() |
| Outside sphere | `ityperest=8` | `outside sphere x y z radius` | Sphere center + radius | [src/getinp.f90:653-658]() |
| Outside ellipsoid | `ityperest=9` | `outside ellipsoid x y z a b c` | Ellipsoid center + semi-axes | [src/getinp.f90:659-667]() |
| Outside cylinder | `ityperest=13` | `outside cylinder x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2 radius length` | Endpoints + radius + length | [src/getinp.f90:668-690]() |
| Above plane | `ityperest=10` | `over plane a b c d` or `above plane a b c d` | Plane equation ax+by+cz=d | [src/getinp.f90:696-711]() |
| Below plane | `ityperest=11` | `below plane a b c d` | Plane equation ax+by+cz=d | [src/getinp.f90:714-729]() |
| Above Gaussian | `ityperest=14` | `over xygauss a b c d sigmax sigmay` | Plane + Gaussian width | [src/getinp.f90:705-708]() |
| Below Gaussian | `ityperest=15` | `below xygauss a b c d sigmax sigmay` | Plane + Gaussian width | [src/getinp.f90:724-726]() |

For detailed constraint evaluation, see [Constraint System Implementation](#7.2).

Sources: [src/getinp.f90:564-737]()

### Atom-Specific Constraints

Constraints can be applied to specific atoms within a molecule using `atoms...end atoms` blocks:

```
structure protein.pdb
  number 1
  atoms 100 101 102 103
    inside sphere 10. 10. 10. 5.
  end atoms
  atoms 200 201 202
    outside sphere 10. 10. 10. 3.
  end atoms
end structure
```

Sources: [src/getinp.f90:566-603](), [app/packmol.f90:563-632]()

---

## Radius and Tolerance Control

### Molecule-Level Radius Settings

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `radius` | `<distance>` | Override default radius (tolerance/2) for all atoms in this molecule. | [app/packmol.f90:317-330]() |
| `fscale` | `<factor>` | Scale factor for distance penalty function. Default: `1.0` | [app/packmol.f90:334-346]() |
| `short_radius` | `<distance>` | Short-range penalty threshold for this molecule. | [app/packmol.f90:351-364]() |
| `short_radius_scale` | `<factor>` | Scale factor for short-range penalty. | [app/packmol.f90:369-382]() |

### Atom-Specific Radius Settings

These same keywords can be used inside `atoms...end atoms` blocks to set atom-specific values:

```
structure complex.pdb
  number 10
  radius 2.5
  atoms 1 2 3
    radius 3.0
    short_radius 1.5
  end atoms
end structure
```

When atom-specific settings are defined, they override molecule-level settings for those atoms.

Sources: [app/packmol.f90:296-515]()

---

## PDB-Specific Options

These options only apply when `filetype pdb`:

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `resnumbers` | `0`\|`1`\|`2`\|`3` | Residue numbering scheme in output. | [src/getinp.f90:825-827]() |
| `changechains` | (none) | Alternate chain identifiers for odd/even molecules. | [src/getinp.f90:822-824]() |
| `chain` | `<character>` | Specific chain identifier for all copies of this molecule. | [src/getinp.f90:833-835]() |
| `segid` | `<string>` | Segment identifier for CRD output. | [src/getinp.f90:836-838]() |
| `connect` | `yes`\|`no` | Whether to write `CONECT` records. Default: `yes` | [src/getinp.f90:828-832]() |

### Residue Numbering Schemes

- `resnumbers 0`: Each molecule gets a unique residue number (1, 2, 3, ...)
- `resnumbers 1`: Use original residue numbers from input file
- `resnumbers 2`: Sequential numbering across all molecules
- `resnumbers 3`: Global molecule index as residue number

Sources: [src/getinp.f90:809-869](), [src/output.f90:270-284]()

---

## Advanced Structure Options

### Restart Files

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `restart_from` | `<filename>` | Read initial positions from file (6 values per molecule: x,y,z,beta,gama,teta). | [src/getinp.f90:898-911]() |
| `restart_to` | `<filename>` | Write final positions to file for later reuse. | [src/getinp.f90:913-927]() |

These can appear either inside a structure block (for one molecule type) or globally (for all types).

### Rotation Constraints

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `constrain_rotation` | `x`\|`y`\|`z` `<min> <max>` | Constrain rotation about specified axis to angle range (degrees). | [app/packmol.f90:643-690]() |

**Example:**
```
structure rod.pdb
  number 100
  constrain_rotation z 0.0 45.0
  inside box 0. 0. 0. 50. 50. 50.
end structure
```

### Other Options

| Keyword | Arguments | Description | Line Reference |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `center` | (none) | Translate molecule center to constraint region centroid before optimization. | Not directly parsed, see code |
| `centerofmass` | (none) | Same as `center` but explicitly uses center of mass. | Not directly parsed, see code |
| `maxmove` | `<integer>` | Maximum number of molecules of this type to move during optimization. Default: all | [src/getinp.f90:795-797]() |
| `nloop` | `<integer>` | Override global `nloop` for this molecule type. | [src/setsizes.f90:257-269]() |
| `nloop0` | `<integer>` | Override global `nloop0` for this molecule type. | [src/setsizes.f90:273-285]() |

Sources: [src/getinp.f90:789-928](), [app/packmol.f90:636-690]()

---

## File Type Support

### PDB Format

Default format. Reads `ATOM` and `HETATM` records, supports `CONECT` records for connectivity.

**Parsing:** [src/getinp.f90:286-381]()  
**Output:** [src/output.f90:134-469]()

### Tinker XYZ Format

Tinker-style XYZ files include atom types and connectivity.

**Parsing:** [src/getinp.f90:384-467]()  
**Output:** [src/output.f90:473-536]()

### Standard XYZ Format

Simple element + coordinates format (no connectivity).

**Parsing:** [src/getinp.f90:470-489]()  
**Output:** [src/output.f90:93-131]()

## Complete Example with Annotations

```
# Global settings
tolerance 2.0              # Required: minimum atom-atom distance
filetype pdb               # Optional: default is pdb
output system.pdb          # Required: output file path
seed 12345                 # Optional: random seed for reproducibility

# Optimization parameters
nloop 500                  # Optional: maximum optimization iterations
precision 0.01             # Optional: convergence threshold
writeout 20                # Optional: write output every 20 iterations

# Periodic boundary conditions
pbc 0.0 0.0 0.0 50.0 50.0 50.0

# Fixed protein structure
structure protein.pdb
  number 1
  fixed 25.0 25.0 25.0 0.0 0.0 0.0  # Center at box center, no rotation
  resnumbers 1             # Keep original residue numbers
  centerofmass
end structure

# Water molecules
structure water.pdb
  number 2000
  inside box 0.0 0.0 0.0 50.0 50.0 50.0
  resnumbers 2             # Sequential numbering
end structure

# Ions confined to central sphere
structure Na.pdb
  number 20
  inside sphere 25.0 25.0 25.0 20.0
  outside sphere 25.0 25.0 25.0 5.0  # Keep away from protein center
end structure

# Lipids with constrained orientation
structure lipid.pdb
  number 100
  constrain_rotation x 0.0 30.0  # Limit rotation about x-axis
  atoms 1 2 3              # Head group atoms
    above plane 0.0 0.0 1.0 20.0  # Force heads above z=20
  end atoms
  radius 2.5               # Override default radius
end structure
```

Sources: [testing/input_files/solvprotein.inp:1-35](), [src/getinp.f90]()

## Keyword Parsing Implementation

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    INPUT_FILE["Input File"] --> SETSIZES["setsizes()"]
    SETSIZES --> READ_LINES["Read all lines<br/>(remove comments)"]
    READ_LINES --> GETKEYWORDS["getkeywords()<br/>Split into keyword array"]
    GETKEYWORDS --> KEYWORD_ARRAY["keyword(nlines, maxkeywords)"]
    
    KEYWORD_ARRAY --> GETINP["getinp()"]
    GETINP --> PARSE_GLOBAL["Parse global keywords"]
    GETINP --> PARSE_STRUCT["Parse structure blocks"]
    GETINP --> VALIDATE["Validate required parameters"]
    
    PARSE_GLOBAL --> SEED_CHECK["Check keyword(i,1)"]
    PARSE_STRUCT --> INSIDE_CHECK["Check for 'structure' keyword"]
    VALIDATE --> TOL_CHECK["Ensure tolerance set"]
    VALIDATE --> OUT_CHECK["Ensure output set"]
    
    SEED_CHECK --> SET_VAR["Set module variable<br/>(e.g., seed, nloop)"]
    INSIDE_CHECK --> READ_FILE["Open and read structure file"]
    TOL_CHECK --> ERROR["Stop with exit_code_input_error"]
```

**Diagram: Keyword Parsing Flow**

The parsing happens in two phases:
1. [src/setsizes.f90:34-137]() reads the input file, removes comments, and splits each line into keywords
2. [src/getinp.f90:9-935]() interprets the keywords and populates module variables

The keyword array is indexed as `keyword(line_number, keyword_position)` where `keyword(i,1)` is the command and `keyword(i,2..n)` are arguments.

Sources: [src/setsizes.f90:9-361](), [src/getinp.f90:9-935]()

| Invalid PBC box dimensions | `exit_code_input_error` | [src/getinp.f90:189-194]() |
| Structure without end statement | `exit_code_input_error` | [src/getinp.f90:800-801]() |

Error messages are written to standard output with explanatory text before termination.

# Page: Spatial Constraints

# Spatial Constraints

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [app/packmol.f90](app/packmol.f90)
- [src/checkpoint.f90](src/checkpoint.f90)
- [src/comprest.f90](src/comprest.f90)
- [src/getinp.f90](src/getinp.f90)
- [src/gwalls.f90](src/gwalls.f90)
- [src/input.f90](src/input.f90)
- [src/output.f90](src/output.f90)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document describes Packmol's spatial constraint system, which allows users to define geometric regions where molecules must be placed (`inside`) or excluded from (`outside`). Spatial constraints are specified in the input file and control molecule placement during the optimization process.

For information about periodic boundary conditions, see [Periodic Boundary Conditions](#3.3). For details on the input file format, see [Input File Format](#3.1).

## Overview

Packmol supports multiple types of spatial constraints that restrict molecule placement to specific geometric regions. Each constraint is defined by a shape (cube, box, sphere, ellipsoid, cylinder, plane, or Gaussian surface) and a direction (inside, outside, above, or below). The optimization engine evaluates these constraints as penalty functions that guide the placement algorithm.

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:576-730](), [src/comprest.f90:1-215]()

## Constraint System Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Processing"
        INPUT_FILE["Input File (.inp)"]
        GETINP["getinp()<br/>src/getinp.f90"]
        KEYWORDS["keyword array<br/>parsed keywords"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Constraint Storage"
        NREST["nrest<br/>total constraint count"]
        ITYPEREST["ityperest(irest)<br/>constraint type codes"]
        RESTPARS["restpars(irest,1:9)<br/>constraint parameters"]
        IRESTLINE["irestline(irest)<br/>input line numbers"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Atom-Level Mapping"
        NRATOM["nratom(icart)<br/>constraints per atom"]
        IRATOM["iratom(icart,i)<br/>constraint indices"]
        ICART["icart<br/>atom index"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Constraint Evaluation"
        COMPREST["comprest(icart,f)<br/>src/comprest.f90"]
        GWALLS["gwalls(icart,irest)<br/>src/gwalls.f90"]
        PENALTY["Penalty Value"]
        GRADIENT["Gradient Vector"]
    end
    
    INPUT_FILE --> GETINP
    GETINP --> KEYWORDS
    KEYWORDS --> NREST
    KEYWORDS --> ITYPEREST
    KEYWORDS --> RESTPARS
    KEYWORDS --> IRESTLINE
    
    ITYPEREST --> NRATOM
    IRESTLINE --> NRATOM
    NRATOM --> IRATOM
    
    ICART --> COMPREST
    NRATOM --> COMPREST
    IRATOM --> COMPREST
    ITYPEREST --> COMPREST
    RESTPARS --> COMPREST
    COMPREST --> PENALTY
    
    ICART --> GWALLS
    IRATOM --> GWALLS
    ITYPEREST --> GWALLS
    RESTPARS --> GWALLS
    GWALLS --> GRADIENT
    
    PENALTY --> OPTIMIZATION["Optimization<br/>GENCAN Solver"]
    GRADIENT --> OPTIMIZATION
```

**Diagram: Spatial Constraint Data Flow**

This diagram shows how constraints flow from input file parsing through storage to evaluation during optimization.

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:558-738](), [app/packmol.f90:548-632](), [src/comprest.f90:11-215](), [src/gwalls.f90:9-327]()

## Constraint Type Codes

Packmol uses numeric type codes (`ityperest`) to identify different constraint types:

| Code | Keyword | Shape | Direction | Description |
|------|---------|-------|-----------|-------------|
| 1 | `fixed` | N/A | N/A | Fixed molecule position and orientation |
| 2 | `inside` | `cube` | Inside | Interior of a cube |
| 3 | `inside` | `box` | Inside | Interior of a rectangular box |
| 4 | `inside` | `sphere` | Inside | Interior of a sphere |
| 5 | `inside` | `ellipsoid` | Inside | Interior of an ellipsoid |
| 6 | `outside` | `cube` | Outside | Exterior of a cube |
| 7 | `outside` | `box` | Outside | Exterior of a rectangular box |
| 8 | `outside` | `sphere` | Outside | Exterior of a sphere |
| 9 | `outside` | `ellipsoid` | Outside | Exterior of an ellipsoid |
| 10 | `over`/`above` | `plane` | Above | Above a plane |
| 11 | `below` | `plane` | Below | Below a plane |
| 12 | `inside` | `cylinder` | Inside | Interior of a cylinder |
| 13 | `outside` | `cylinder` | Outside | Exterior of a cylinder |
| 14 | `over`/`above` | `xygauss` | Above | Above a Gaussian surface on XY plane |
| 15 | `below` | `xygauss` | Below | Below a Gaussian surface on XY plane |

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:564-730](), [src/comprest.f90:24-212]()

## Input File Specification

Constraints are specified in the input file within structure blocks. They can be applied to entire molecules or specific atoms.

### Molecule-Level Constraints

```
structure water.pdb
  number 1000
  inside box 0. 0. 0. 50. 50. 50.
end structure
```

### Atom-Level Constraints

```
structure protein.pdb
  number 1
  atoms 1 2 3 4 5
    inside sphere 10. 10. 10. 15.
  end atoms
  atoms 6 7 8
    outside cube 0. 0. 0. 5.
  end atoms
end structure
```

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:564-615](), [app/packmol.f90:563-616]()

## Constraint Parameter Storage

The `restpars(irest,1:9)` array stores geometric parameters for each constraint. The meaning of each index depends on the constraint type:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Inside/Outside Cube"
        CUBE_PARAMS["restpars(irest,:)<br/>1: xmin<br/>2: ymin<br/>3: zmin<br/>4: cube_length"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Inside/Outside Box"
        BOX_PARAMS["restpars(irest,:)<br/>1: xmin<br/>2: ymin<br/>3: zmin<br/>4: xmax<br/>5: ymax<br/>6: zmax"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Inside/Outside Sphere"
        SPHERE_PARAMS["restpars(irest,:)<br/>1: x_center<br/>2: y_center<br/>3: z_center<br/>4: radius"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Inside/Outside Ellipsoid"
        ELLIPSOID_PARAMS["restpars(irest,:)<br/>1: x_center<br/>2: y_center<br/>3: z_center<br/>4: a_axis<br/>5: b_axis<br/>6: c_axis<br/>7: scale_factor"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Inside/Outside Cylinder"
        CYLINDER_PARAMS["restpars(irest,:)<br/>1: x_base<br/>2: y_base<br/>3: z_base<br/>4-6: direction_vector<br/>7: radius<br/>8: norm_squared<br/>9: length"]
    end
```

## Constraint Parsing Details

```mermaid

    CHECK_KEYWORD -->|Yes| INSIDE
    CHECK_KEYWORD -->|Yes| OUTSIDE
    CHECK_KEYWORD -->|Yes| ABOVE
    CHECK_KEYWORD -->|Yes| BELOW
    CHECK_KEYWORD -->|No| SCAN_LINES
    
    INSIDE --> CHECK_SHAPE
    OUTSIDE --> CHECK_SHAPE
    CHECK_SHAPE --> CUBE
    CHECK_SHAPE --> BOX
    CHECK_SHAPE --> SPHERE
    CHECK_SHAPE --> ELLIPSOID
    CHECK_SHAPE --> CYLINDER
    
    ABOVE --> PLANE
    ABOVE --> XYGAUSS
    BELOW --> PLANE
    BELOW --> XYGAUSS
    
    FIXED --> READ_PARAMS
    CUBE --> READ_PARAMS
    BOX --> READ_PARAMS
    SPHERE --> READ_PARAMS
    ELLIPSOID --> READ_PARAMS
    CYLINDER --> READ_PARAMS
    PLANE --> READ_PARAMS
    XYGAUSS --> READ_PARAMS
    
    READ_PARAMS --> NORMALIZE
    NORMALIZE --> STORE
    STORE --> INCREMENT
    INCREMENT --> SCAN_LINES
```

## Atom-to-Constraint Mapping

After parsing all constraints, Packmol maps each atom to the constraints that apply to it. This mapping is stored in the `nratom` and `iratom` arrays.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Structure Definition"
        STRUCTURE["structure block<br/>linestrut(itype,1:2)"]
        MOL_CONSTRAINT["Molecule-level<br/>constraint"]
        ATOM_BLOCK["atoms block<br/>specific atom indices"]
        ATOM_CONSTRAINT["Atom-level<br/>constraint"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Mapping Loop"
        ITYPE["Loop itype = 1:ntype"]
        IMOL["Loop imol = 1:nmols(itype)"]
        IATOM["Loop iatom = 1:natoms(itype)"]
        ICART_CALC["icart index calculation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Constraint Assignment"
        CHECK_LINE{"Is iline within<br/>structure bounds?"}
        CHECK_ATOMS{"Inside atoms block?"}
        MATCH_ATOM{"iatom matches<br/>atom selection?"}
        ADD_CONSTRAINT["nratom(icart)++<br/>iratom(icart,i) = irest"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Result"
        NRATOM_ARR["nratom(icart)<br/>count of constraints"]
        IRATOM_ARR["iratom(icart,1:nratom)<br/>constraint indices"]
    end
    
    STRUCTURE --> ITYPE
    ITYPE --> IMOL
    IMOL --> IATOM
    IATOM --> ICART_CALC
    ICART_CALC --> CHECK_LINE
    
    CHECK_LINE -->|Yes| CHECK_ATOMS
    CHECK_LINE -->|No| IATOM
    
    CHECK_ATOMS -->|No| MOL_CONSTRAINT
    CHECK_ATOMS -->|Yes| MATCH_ATOM
    
    MOL_CONSTRAINT --> ADD_CONSTRAINT
    MATCH_ATOM -->|Yes| ATOM_CONSTRAINT
    ATOM_CONSTRAINT --> ADD_CONSTRAINT
    
    ADD_CONSTRAINT --> NRATOM_ARR
    ADD_CONSTRAINT --> IRATOM_ARR
```

**Diagram: Atom-to-Constraint Mapping Process**

**Sources:** [app/packmol.f90:550-632]()

## Constraint Evaluation: comprest()

The `comprest()` subroutine evaluates constraint violations for a single atom and returns a penalty value. The penalty is zero when the constraint is satisfied and increases quadratically with the distance from the constraint boundary.

### Evaluation Strategy by Type

**Inside Constraints (types 2-5, 12):** Penalty when atom is outside the region
```fortran
! Example: inside sphere (type 4)
w = (x - x_center)^2 + (y - y_center)^2 + (z - z_center)^2 - radius^2
penalty = scale2 * max(w, 0)^2
```

**Outside Constraints (types 6-9, 13):** Penalty when atom is inside the region
```fortran
! Example: outside sphere (type 8)
w = (x - x_center)^2 + (y - y_center)^2 + (z - z_center)^2 - radius^2
penalty = scale2 * min(w, 0)^2
```

**Above/Below Plane (types 10-11):** Penalty based on signed distance to plane
```fortran
! Example: above plane (type 10)
w = a*x + b*y + c*z - d  ! signed distance
penalty = scale * min(w, 0)^2  ! penalty if below plane
```

**Sources:** [src/comprest.f90:11-215]()

## Constraint Types in Detail

### Fixed Position (type 1)

Fixed molecules are positioned at exact coordinates with specific orientation specified by Euler angles. This is handled specially in the main program, not in `comprest`.

**Input Format:**
```
structure molecule.pdb
  number 1
  fixed x y z alpha beta gamma
end structure
```

**Parameters:**
- `restpars(irest,1:3)`: center of mass coordinates (x, y, z)
- `restpars(irest,4:6)`: Euler angles (alpha, beta, gamma) in degrees

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:564-574](), [app/packmol.f90:117-162]()

### Cube Constraints (types 2, 6)

A cube is defined by its minimum corner and side length.

**Input Format:**
```
inside cube xmin ymin zmin length
outside cube xmin ymin zmin length
```

**Evaluation:** For inside cube (type 2), penalty is applied if any coordinate is outside `[xmin, xmin+length]` etc.

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:579-584](), [src/comprest.f90:29-44](), [src/gwalls.f90:24-43]()

### Box Constraints (types 3, 7)

A box is defined by minimum and maximum coordinates in each dimension.

**Input Format:**
```
inside box xmin ymin zmin xmax ymax zmax
outside box xmin ymin zmin xmax ymax zmax
```

**Evaluation:** For inside box (type 3), penalty is applied if any coordinate is outside its respective bounds.

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:585-592](), [src/comprest.f90:45-59](), [src/gwalls.f90:44-63]()

### Sphere Constraints (types 4, 8)

A sphere is defined by its center and radius.

**Input Format:**
```
inside sphere x_center y_center z_center radius
outside sphere x_center y_center z_center radius
```

**Evaluation Formula:**
```
distance_squared = (x - x_center)² + (y - y_center)² + (z - z_center)²
for inside: penalty if distance_squared > radius²
for outside: penalty if distance_squared < radius²
```

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:593-598](), [src/comprest.f90:60-66](), [src/gwalls.f90:63-75]()

### Ellipsoid Constraints (types 5, 9)

An ellipsoid is defined by its center, three semi-axes, and a scale factor.

**Input Format:**
```
inside ellipsoid x_center y_center z_center a b c scale
outside ellipsoid x_center y_center z_center a b c scale
```

**Evaluation Formula:**
```
w = (x - x_center)²/a² + (y - y_center)²/b² + (z - z_center)²/c² - scale²
for inside: penalty if w > 0
for outside: penalty if w < 0
```

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:599-607](), [src/comprest.f90:67-74](), [src/gwalls.f90:76-88]()

### Cylinder Constraints (types 12, 13)

A cylinder is defined by a base point, direction vector, radius, and length.

**Input Format:**
```
inside cylinder x y z vx vy vz radius length
outside cylinder x y z vx vy vz radius length
```

**Parameters:**
- `restpars(irest,1:3)`: base point coordinates
- `restpars(irest,4:6)`: direction vector (normalized during parsing)
- `restpars(irest,7)`: radius
- `restpars(irest,8)`: squared norm (computed, used for normalization)
- `restpars(irest,9)`: length along axis

**Evaluation:** Checks both radial distance from axis and axial position within `[0, length]`.

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:608-630](), [src/comprest.f90:158-174](), [src/gwalls.f90:202-242]()

### Plane Constraints (types 10, 11)

A plane is defined by its normal vector (a, b, c) and offset d, representing the equation `ax + by + cz = d`.

**Input Format:**
```
above plane a b c d
below plane a b c d
```

**Evaluation:**
```
signed_distance = a*x + b*y + c*z - d
for above: penalty if signed_distance < 0
for below: penalty if signed_distance > 0
```

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:696-712](), [src/comprest.f90:144-157](), [src/gwalls.f90:180-201]()

### Gaussian Surface Constraints (types 14, 15)

A Gaussian surface on the XY plane is defined by the equation:
```
z = h * exp(-(x-a)²/(2c²) - (y-b)²/(2d²)) + g
```

**Input Format:**
```
above xygauss a b c d g h
below xygauss a b c d g h
```

**Parameters:**
- `restpars(irest,1:2)`: center coordinates (a, b) on XY plane
- `restpars(irest,3:4)`: standard deviations (c, d) for X and Y
- `restpars(irest,5)`: base height (g)
- `restpars(irest,6)`: amplitude (h)

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:703-730](), [src/comprest.f90:192-212](), [src/gwalls.f90:291-323]()

## Gradient Computation: gwalls()

The `gwalls()` subroutine computes the gradient of the constraint penalty with respect to the atom's Cartesian coordinates. These gradients are accumulated in the `gxcar(icart,1:3)` array.

### Gradient Pattern

For quadratic penalties of the form `f = scale * (expression)²`, the gradient follows the chain rule:
```
∂f/∂x = 2 * scale * expression * (∂expression/∂x)
```

### Example: Inside Box

```fortran
! For coordinate violations
if (x < xmin) then
    gxcar(icart,1) = gxcar(icart,1) + scale * 2.0 * (x - xmin)
end if
if (x > xmax) then
    gxcar(icart,1) = gxcar(icart,1) + scale * 2.0 * (x - xmax)
end if
```

**Sources:** [src/gwalls.f90:9-327]()

## Constraint Scaling Factors

Packmol uses two scaling factors for constraint penalties:

| Variable | Value | Used For |
|----------|-------|----------|
| `scale` | 1000.0 | Box/cube constraints (types 2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 14, 15) |
| `scale2` | 100.0 | Sphere/ellipsoid/cylinder constraints (types 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 13) |

These are defined in the `compute_data` module and ensure constraint violations contribute significantly to the objective function.

**Sources:** [src/comprest.f90:14](), [src/compute_data.f90]()

## Periodic Boundary Conditions Integration

When periodic boundary conditions (PBC) are enabled, Packmol automatically adds an `inside box` constraint to ensure all atoms remain within the PBC box:

```fortran
if (using_pbc) then
    nrest = nrest + 1
    irestline(nrest) = -1  ! special marker for auto-generated constraint
    ityperest(nrest) = 3   ! inside box
    restpars(nrest,1:3) = pbc_min
    restpars(nrest,4:6) = pbc_max
end if
```

This constraint is automatically applied to all non-fixed atoms during the atom-to-constraint mapping phase.

**Sources:** [app/packmol.f90:530-546](), [app/packmol.f90:617-623]()

## Multiple Constraints Per Atom

An atom can have multiple constraints applied simultaneously. The total penalty for an atom is the sum of all individual constraint penalties:

```fortran
f = 0.d0
do iratcount = 1, nratom(icart)
    irest = iratom(icart,iratcount)
    ! Add penalty for constraint irest
    f = f + penalty_for_constraint(irest)
end do
```

During optimization, all constraints must be satisfied for the solution to be valid.

**Sources:** [src/comprest.f90:26-28](), [src/comprest.f90:213-215]()

## Constraint Application Workflow

```mermaid
graph TB
    START["Molecule Placement<br/>Optimization Loop"]
    
    subgraph "Per-Iteration"
        COMPUTEF["computef(n,x,fx)<br/>Evaluate objective"]
        LOOP_ATOMS["Loop over atoms<br/>icart = 1:ntotat"]
        COMPREST_CALL["comprest(icart, f)<br/>Sum constraint penalties"]
        ACCUMULATE["fx += f"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Gradient Computation"
        COMPUTEG["computeg(n,x,g)<br/>Compute gradient"]
        LOOP_ATOMS_G["Loop over atoms<br/>icart = 1:ntotat"]
        GWALLS_CALL["For each constraint:<br/>gwalls(icart, irest)"]
        ACCUMULATE_G["Accumulate in gxcar"]
    end
    
    GENCAN["GENCAN Solver<br/>Update positions"]
    CONVERGED{"Constraints<br/>satisfied?"}
    OUTPUT["Write output file"]
    
    START --> COMPUTEF
    COMPUTEF --> LOOP_ATOMS
    LOOP_ATOMS --> COMPREST_CALL
    COMPREST_CALL --> ACCUMULATE
    ACCUMULATE --> LOOP_ATOMS
    
    ACCUMULATE --> COMPUTEG
    COMPUTEG --> LOOP_ATOMS_G
    LOOP_ATOMS_G --> GWALLS_CALL
    GWALLS_CALL --> ACCUMULATE_G
    ACCUMULATE_G --> LOOP_ATOMS_G
    
    ACCUMULATE_G --> GENCAN
    GENCAN --> CONVERGED
    CONVERGED -->|No| COMPUTEF
    CONVERGED -->|Yes| OUTPUT
```

**Diagram: Constraint Evaluation in Optimization Loop**

**Sources:** [src/computef.f90](), [src/computeg.f90](), [app/packmol.f90:740-850]()

## Special Considerations

### Outside Constraints Implementation

Outside constraints (types 6-9, 13) require special handling. For cubes and boxes, the penalty computation identifies the nearest face and applies a linear penalty (not quadratic) to push atoms away from the interior:

```fortran
! For outside cube/box, find minimum distance to push out
if (inside region) then
    ! Find which face is closest
    xmed = (xmax - xmin) / 2
    if (x <= xmed) a1 = x - xmin  ! distance to left face
    if (x > xmed) a1 = xmax - x   ! distance to right face
    ! Similar for y and z
    f = f + scale * (a1 + a2 + a3)  ! sum of distances
end if
```

**Sources:** [src/comprest.f90:75-101](), [src/gwalls.f90:89-120]()

### Cylinder Direction Vector Normalization

When parsing cylinder constraints, the direction vector is automatically normalized:

```fortran
restpars(irest,8) = vx^2 + vy^2 + vz^2  ! store squared norm
clen = sqrt(restpars(irest,8))
restpars(irest,4:6) = restpars(irest,4:6) / clen  ! normalize
```

This ensures consistent behavior regardless of the input vector magnitude.

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:618-630]()

### Constraint Error Checking

The input parser validates constraint specifications and exits with informative error messages if constraints are malformed:

```fortran
if (ioerr /= 0) then
    write(*,*) ' ERROR: Some restriction is not set correctly. '
    stop exit_code_input_error
end if
```

Common errors include invalid numeric values, missing parameters, or unrecognized shape keywords.

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:732-735]()

# Page: Periodic Boundary Conditions

# Periodic Boundary Conditions

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [CMakeLists.txt](CMakeLists.txt)
- [src/cell_indexing.f90](src/cell_indexing.f90)
- [src/pbc.f90](src/pbc.f90)
- [src/resetcells.f90](src/resetcells.f90)
- [testing/input_files/water_box.inp](testing/input_files/water_box.inp)
- [testing/input_files/water_box_pbc.inp](testing/input_files/water_box_pbc.inp)
- [testing/input_files/water_box_pbc_negative_coordinates.inp](testing/input_files/water_box_pbc_negative_coordinates.inp)
- [testing/input_files/water_box_pbc_slab.inp](testing/input_files/water_box_pbc_slab.inp)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents Packmol's support for periodic boundary conditions (PBC), which allows molecular systems to be packed in a periodic simulation box. This feature is essential for preparing systems for molecular dynamics simulations with periodic boundary conditions.

This page covers:
- Enabling PBC in input files using the `pbc` keyword
- The PBC implementation in the `pbc` module
- Coordinate wrapping and minimum image convention
- Integration with the spatial cell indexing system

For information about spatial constraints without PBC, see [Spatial Constraints](#3.2). For details on the cell indexing system that PBC integrates with, see [Spatial Management System](#4.5).

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90](), [testing/input_files/water_box_pbc.inp]()

## Overview

Periodic boundary conditions simulate an infinite system by replicating a finite simulation box in all three dimensions. When a molecule or atom moves out of one side of the box, it reappears on the opposite side. This eliminates surface effects and allows simulation of bulk systems with a finite number of particles.

In Packmol, PBC affects:
- **Distance calculations**: Distances are computed using the minimum image convention
- **Cell indexing**: Cell indices wrap around at box boundaries
- **Coordinate wrapping**: Molecule centers are wrapped into the primary simulation box

The PBC system is controlled by the `using_pbc` flag and defined by box parameters `pbc_min`, `pbc_max`, and `pbc_length`.

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:1-31]()

## Enabling PBC in Input Files

### The `pbc` Keyword

PBC is enabled in input files using the `pbc` keyword, which can be specified in two formats:

**Format 1: Box lengths only**
```
pbc Lx Ly Lz
```
This defines a periodic box with dimensions `Lx × Ly × Lz`, with the origin at (0, 0, 0).

**Format 2: Explicit box boundaries**
```
pbc xmin ymin zmin xmax ymax zmax
```
This defines a periodic box from `(xmin, ymin, zmin)` to `(xmax, ymax, zmax)`.

### Example Input Files

| Input File | Box Definition | Description |
|------------|----------------|-------------|
| `water_box_pbc.inp` | `pbc 40. 40. 40.` | Cubic box 40×40×40, origin at (0,0,0) |
| `water_box_pbc_negative_coordinates.inp` | `pbc -20. -20. -20. 20. 20. 20.` | Cubic box 40×40×40, centered at origin |
| `water_box_pbc_slab.inp` | `pbc 40.0 40.0 40.0` with exclusion sphere | PBC with interior void region |

### Combining PBC with Constraints

PBC can be combined with spatial constraints such as `inside` or `outside` directives. For example, creating a slab geometry:

```
pbc 40.0 40.0 40.0
structure water.pdb
  number 1000
  outside sphere 20. 20. 20. 10.0
end structure
```

This creates a periodic box with water molecules everywhere except inside a central sphere, useful for simulating interfaces or porous materials.

**Sources:** [testing/input_files/water_box_pbc.inp:1-18](), [testing/input_files/water_box_pbc_negative_coordinates.inp:1-17](), [testing/input_files/water_box_pbc_slab.inp:1-18]()

## PBC Module Architecture

The PBC functionality is implemented in the `pbc` module, which provides a public interface of three elemental functions and three public variables.

### PBC Module Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "pbc Module"
        FLAG["using_pbc<br/>(logical)"]
        MIN["pbc_min(3)<br/>(box minimum)"]
        MAX["pbc_max(3)<br/>(box maximum)"]
        LEN["pbc_length(3)<br/>(box dimensions)"]
        
        V_IN_BOX["v_in_box()<br/>(wrap coordinate)"]
        DELTA["delta_vector()<br/>(minimum image distance)"]
        CELL_IND["cell_ind()<br/>(wrap cell index)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Client Modules"
        SETCELL["cell_indexing::setcell<br/>(assign atoms to cells)"]
        FPARC["fparc.f90<br/>(distance objective)"]
        GPARC["gparc.f90<br/>(distance gradient)"]
    end
    
    FLAG --> SETCELL
    FLAG --> FPARC
    FLAG --> GPARC
    
    MIN --> V_IN_BOX
    LEN --> V_IN_BOX
    V_IN_BOX --> SETCELL
    
    LEN --> DELTA
    DELTA --> FPARC
    DELTA --> GPARC
    
    CELL_IND --> SETCELL
    
    style FLAG fill:#f9f9f9
    style V_IN_BOX fill:#f9f9f9
    style DELTA fill:#f9f9f9
    style CELL_IND fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Diagram: PBC Module Interface and Dependencies**

The module exports:
- **State Variables**: `using_pbc`, `pbc_min(3)`, `pbc_max(3)`, `pbc_length(3)`
- **Functions**: `v_in_box`, `delta_vector`, `cell_ind`

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:5-31]()

## Coordinate Wrapping: `v_in_box`

The `v_in_box` function wraps a single coordinate component into the periodic box using the modulo operation.

### Function Signature

```fortran
elemental double precision function v_in_box(v, pbc_min, pbc_length)
```

### Implementation

[src/pbc.f90:15-18]()

The function uses the modulo operation to compute:
```
v_in_box = pbc_min + modulo((v - pbc_min), pbc_length)
```

This ensures that the wrapped coordinate satisfies:
```
pbc_min ≤ v_in_box < pbc_min + pbc_length
```

### Usage in Cell Indexing

The `setcell` subroutine uses `v_in_box` to wrap atom coordinates before assigning them to cells:

[src/cell_indexing.f90:14-25]()

The wrapping sequence is:
1. Apply `v_in_box` to all three coordinate components
2. Compute cell indices based on wrapped coordinates
3. Apply safeguard for coordinates exactly at `pbc_max`

```mermaid
graph LR
    INPUT["Input coordinate<br/>x(3)"]
    WRAP["v_in_box(x, pbc_min, pbc_length)<br/>→ xt(3)"]
    FLOOR["floor((xt - pbc_min) / cell_length) + 1<br/>→ cell(3)"]
    SAFEGUARD["min(cell, ncells)<br/>→ final cell(3)"]
    
    INPUT --> WRAP
    WRAP --> FLOOR
    FLOOR --> SAFEGUARD
```

**Diagram: Coordinate to Cell Index Conversion with PBC**

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:15-18](), [src/cell_indexing.f90:14-25]()

## Distance Calculation: `delta_vector`

The `delta_vector` function computes the distance vector between two coordinates using the minimum image convention, which ensures that the shortest distance across periodic boundaries is calculated.

### Function Signature

```fortran
elemental double precision function delta_vector(v1, v2, pbc_length)
```

### Implementation

[src/pbc.f90:20-24]()

The function implements the minimum image convention:
```
delta = v1 - v2
delta = delta - pbc_length * nint(delta / pbc_length)
```

The `nint` (nearest integer) function rounds `delta / pbc_length` to the nearest integer, effectively shifting the distance vector by the appropriate number of box lengths to find the minimum image.

### Minimum Image Convention

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Periodic Box (1D Example)"
        BOX1["[-L/2, L/2]"]
        
        PARTICLE1["Particle 1<br/>position: -0.4L"]
        PARTICLE2["Particle 2<br/>position: +0.4L"]
        
        DIRECT["Direct distance:<br/>Δ = 0.8L"]
        IMAGE["Image distance:<br/>Δ = -0.2L (minimum)"]
    end
    
    PARTICLE1 --> DIRECT
    PARTICLE2 --> DIRECT
    DIRECT --> CHOICE{"|Δ| > L/2?"}
    CHOICE -->|Yes| SHIFT["Shift by ±L:<br/>Δ_min = Δ - L*nint(Δ/L)"]
    CHOICE -->|No| KEEP["Keep Δ"]
    SHIFT --> IMAGE
    KEEP --> IMAGE
```

**Diagram: Minimum Image Convention in 1D**

### Example Calculation

For a box of length L = 10:
- Particle 1 at x₁ = 9.5
- Particle 2 at x₂ = 0.5
- Direct distance: Δ = 9.5 - 0.5 = 9.0
- Wrapped distance: Δ = 9.0 - 10 × nint(9.0/10) = 9.0 - 10 × 1 = -1.0

The minimum image distance is 1.0 (magnitude), indicating the particles are neighbors across the periodic boundary.

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:20-24]()

## Cell Index Wrapping: `cell_ind`

The `cell_ind` function wraps cell indices to account for periodic boundary conditions in the cell grid.

### Function Signature

```fortran
integer function cell_ind(icell, ncells)
```

### Implementation

[src/pbc.f90:26-29]()

The function uses modulo arithmetic to wrap cell indices:
```
cell_ind = modulo(icell - 1 + ncells, ncells) + 1
```

This ensures cell indices are in the range `[1, ncells]`, handling both positive and negative input indices correctly.

### Usage Pattern

When searching neighboring cells in the 3×3×3 stencil around a cell, indices may fall outside the valid range. The `cell_ind` function wraps them back:

```
! Example: neighbor search in x-direction
do ix = cell(1) - 1, cell(1) + 1
   icellx = cell_ind(ix, ncells(1))  ! Wrap if ix < 1 or ix > ncells(1)
   ! ... process neighbor cell
end do
```

### Cell Index Wrapping Illustration

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Cell Grid (1D)"
        C1["Cell 1"]
        C2["Cell 2"]
        C3["Cell 3"]
        CDOTS["..."]
        CN["Cell N"]
    end
    
    LEFT["icell = 0<br/>wraps to N"]
    RIGHT["icell = N+1<br/>wraps to 1"]
    
    LEFT -.->|"cell_ind"| CN
    RIGHT -.->|"cell_ind"| C1
    C1 <-.->|"periodic"| CN
```

**Diagram: Cell Index Wrapping at Boundaries**

The wrapping ensures that:
- `cell_ind(0, N) = N` (left boundary wraps to right)
- `cell_ind(N+1, N) = 1` (right boundary wraps to left)
- `cell_ind(k, N) = k` for `1 ≤ k ≤ N` (interior cells unchanged)

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:26-29]()

## Integration with Spatial Cell Indexing

The PBC module integrates tightly with Packmol's spatial cell indexing system, which partitions the simulation box into a 3D grid for efficient neighbor searching.

### Cell Setup with PBC

When PBC is enabled, the cell grid spans the entire periodic box defined by `pbc_min` and `pbc_max`. The cell length is chosen based on the interaction cutoff radius:

```
cell_length = radius + tolerance
ncells = ceiling((pbc_max - pbc_min) / cell_length)
```

### Cell Assignment with Wrapping

The `setcell` subroutine in [src/cell_indexing.f90:14-25]() demonstrates the integration:

1. **Coordinate Wrapping**: Apply `v_in_box` to wrap coordinates into the periodic box
2. **Cell Index Calculation**: Compute cell indices based on wrapped coordinates
3. **Boundary Safeguard**: Apply `min(cell, ncells)` to handle edge case at `pbc_max`

### PBC-Aware Neighbor Search

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Neighbor Search with PBC"
        START["Start at cell (ix, iy, iz)"]
        LOOP["Loop over 3×3×3 stencil<br/>(27 neighboring cells)"]
        
        OFFSET["Compute neighbor indices:<br/>ix_n = ix + dx<br/>iy_n = iy + dy<br/>iz_n = iz + dz"]
        
        WRAP["Apply cell_ind wrapping:<br/>ix_w = cell_ind(ix_n, ncells(1))<br/>iy_w = cell_ind(iy_n, ncells(2))<br/>iz_w = cell_ind(iz_n, ncells(3))"]
        
        ACCESS["Access wrapped cell:<br/>latomfirst(ix_w, iy_w, iz_w)"]
        
        DISTANCE["Calculate distances:<br/>use delta_vector for PBC"]
    end
    
    START --> LOOP
    LOOP --> OFFSET
    OFFSET --> WRAP
    WRAP --> ACCESS
    ACCESS --> DISTANCE
    DISTANCE --> LOOP
```

**Diagram: Neighbor Search Algorithm with PBC**

The key steps are:
1. Iterate over the 3×3×3 cell stencil centered on the current cell
2. Wrap neighbor cell indices using `cell_ind` to handle periodic boundaries
3. Access the wrapped cell using the linked list structure
4. Calculate atom-atom distances using `delta_vector` for minimum image distances

**Sources:** [src/cell_indexing.f90:14-25](), [src/pbc.f90:26-29]()

## PBC Data Flow

The following diagram shows how PBC information flows through the system during a typical optimization iteration:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    INPUT["Input file parsing<br/>getinp.f90"]
    
    INIT_PBC["Initialize PBC parameters<br/>using_pbc = .true.<br/>pbc_min, pbc_max, pbc_length"]
    
    INIT_CELLS["Initialize cell grid<br/>initial.f90"]
    
    RESET["Reset cell occupancy<br/>resetcells.f90"]
    
    SETCELL["Assign atoms to cells<br/>setcell() with v_in_box"]
    
    COMPUTE["Compute objective/gradient<br/>computef/computeg"]
    
    FPARC["Distance calculations<br/>fparc.f90 with delta_vector"]
    
    GPARC["Gradient calculations<br/>gparc.f90 with delta_vector"]
    
    UPDATE["GENCAN updates positions"]
    
    WRAP_CHECK{"Positions<br/>outside box?"}
    
    WRAP_COORDS["Apply v_in_box<br/>to wrap coordinates"]
    
    INPUT --> INIT_PBC
    INIT_PBC --> INIT_CELLS
    INIT_CELLS --> RESET
    RESET --> SETCELL
    SETCELL --> COMPUTE
    COMPUTE --> FPARC
    COMPUTE --> GPARC
    FPARC --> UPDATE
    GPARC --> UPDATE
    UPDATE --> WRAP_CHECK
    WRAP_CHECK -->|Yes| WRAP_COORDS
    WRAP_CHECK -->|No| RESET
    WRAP_COORDS --> RESET
```

**Diagram: PBC Data Flow During Optimization**

Throughout the optimization:
- `v_in_box` keeps molecule centers within the periodic box
- `delta_vector` ensures all distance calculations use minimum image convention
- `cell_ind` enables seamless neighbor searching across periodic boundaries

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:5-31](), [src/cell_indexing.f90:14-25](), [src/resetcells.f90:10-42]()

## Comparison: PBC vs Non-PBC Systems

| Aspect | Without PBC | With PBC |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| **Box Definition** | Constraints define packing region | `pbc` keyword defines simulation box |
| **Distance Calculation** | Direct Euclidean distance | Minimum image convention via `delta_vector` |
| **Coordinate Range** | Unbounded (within constraints) | Wrapped to `[pbc_min, pbc_max)` via `v_in_box` |
| **Cell Indexing** | Standard array indexing | Wrapped indexing via `cell_ind` |
| **Neighbor Search** | Boundary cells have fewer neighbors | All cells have full 27-neighbor stencil |
| **Typical Use Case** | Isolated molecules, proteins in solution | Bulk liquids, crystals, membranes |

### Example Comparison

**Non-PBC Input** ([testing/input_files/water_box.inp]()):
```
structure ./structure_files/water.pdb
  number 1000
  inside box -20. -20. -20. 20. 20. 20.
end structure
```

**PBC Input** ([testing/input_files/water_box_pbc.inp]()):
```
pbc 40. 40. 40.
structure ./structure_files/water.pdb
  number 1150
end structure
```

The PBC version can pack more molecules (1150 vs 1000) in the same volume because:
- No surface effects reduce packing efficiency
- All molecules have full coordination environment
- Edge molecules don't preferentially pack toward the center

**Sources:** [testing/input_files/water_box.inp:1-15](), [testing/input_files/water_box_pbc.inp:1-18]()

## Technical Implementation Details

### Elemental Functions

All three PBC functions (`v_in_box`, `delta_vector`, `cell_ind`) are declared as `elemental`, meaning they can operate on scalar or array arguments element-wise. This enables efficient vectorized operations:

```fortran
! Single coordinate wrapping
x_wrapped = v_in_box(x, pbc_min(1), pbc_length(1))

! Vector wrapping (element-wise)
xt(1:3) = v_in_box(x(1:3), pbc_min(1:3), pbc_length(1:3))
```

### Module Dependencies

```mermaid
graph TB
    PBC["pbc module<br/>(src/pbc.f90)"]
    
    CELL_IDX["cell_indexing module<br/>(src/cell_indexing.f90)"]
    
    COMPUTE["compute_data module<br/>(src/compute_data.f90)"]
    
    FPARC["fparc.f90<br/>(objective function)"]
    
    GPARC["gparc.f90<br/>(gradient)"]
    
    RESET["resetcells.f90<br/>(cell reset)"]
    
    PBC --> CELL_IDX
    PBC --> FPARC
    PBC --> GPARC
    
    CELL_IDX --> RESET
    COMPUTE --> RESET
    
    style PBC fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Diagram: Module Dependency Graph for PBC**

The `pbc` module has no dependencies, making it a low-level utility module. Higher-level modules import and use its functions for coordinate wrapping, distance calculations, and cell index management.

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:1-31](), [src/cell_indexing.f90:1-63](), [src/resetcells.f90:1-43]()

---

# Page: Output File Formats

# Output File Formats

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [app/packmol.f90](app/packmol.f90)
- [src/checkpoint.f90](src/checkpoint.f90)
- [src/getinp.f90](src/getinp.f90)
- [src/input.f90](src/input.f90)
- [src/output.f90](src/output.f90)

</details>



This page documents the output file formats supported by Packmol and the options available for customizing the generated structure files. For information about input file syntax, see [Input File Format](#3.1). For command-line usage, see [Command-Line Interface](#3.5).

## Purpose and Scope

Packmol generates molecular structure files in multiple formats suitable for molecular dynamics simulation packages. The output generation process is implemented in [src/output.f90]() and controlled by keywords in the input file. This page covers:

- Supported output file formats (PDB, Tinker XYZ, standard XYZ, CHARMM CRD)
- Format-specific options and customization
- Residue numbering schemes
- Connectivity information handling
- Restart file generation

## Supported Output Formats

Packmol supports four primary output formats, controlled by the `filetype` keyword in the input file:

| Format | Keyword | File Extension | Primary Use Case |
|--------|---------|----------------|------------------|
| PDB | `filetype pdb` | `.pdb` | Protein Data Bank format, widely used for biomolecular simulations |
| Tinker XYZ | `filetype tinker` | `.xyz` | Tinker molecular modeling package format with connectivity |
| Standard XYZ | `filetype xyz` | `.xyz` | Simple Cartesian coordinate format |
| CHARMM CRD | `writecrd <file>` | `.crd` | CHARMM coordinate format (supplemental to PDB) |

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:1-599](), [src/getinp.f90:146-149]()

### Format Selection Logic

```mermaid
graph TD
    START["Input File Processing<br/>getinp.f90"] --> CHECK_FILETYPE["Check 'filetype' keyword<br/>getinp.f90:setsizes"]
    CHECK_FILETYPE --> PDB_CHECK{"filetype == 'pdb'?"}
    CHECK_FILETYPE --> TINKER_CHECK{"filetype == 'tinker'?"}
    CHECK_FILETYPE --> XYZ_CHECK{"filetype == 'xyz'?"}
    
    PDB_CHECK -->|Yes| SET_PDB["pdb = .true.<br/>input.f90"]
    TINKER_CHECK -->|Yes| SET_TINKER["tinker = .true.<br/>input.f90"]
    XYZ_CHECK -->|Yes| SET_XYZ["xyz = .true.<br/>input.f90"]
    
    SET_PDB --> CHECK_CRD{"writecrd keyword?"}
    CHECK_CRD -->|Yes| SET_CRD["crd = .true.<br/>getinp.f90:146-149"]
    CHECK_CRD -->|No| OUTPUT_CALL
    SET_CRD --> OUTPUT_CALL
    SET_TINKER --> OUTPUT_CALL
    SET_XYZ --> OUTPUT_CALL
    
    OUTPUT_CALL["output subroutine<br/>output.f90:9"] --> WRITE_RESTART["Write restart files<br/>output.f90:46-89"]
    WRITE_RESTART --> FORMAT_BRANCH{"Which format?"}
    
    FORMAT_BRANCH -->|xyz| WRITE_XYZ["Write XYZ output<br/>output.f90:93-131"]
    FORMAT_BRANCH -->|pdb| WRITE_PDB["Write PDB output<br/>output.f90:134-469"]
    FORMAT_BRANCH -->|tinker| WRITE_TINKER["Write Tinker output<br/>output.f90:473-536"]
    
    WRITE_PDB --> CHECK_CRD_OUT{"crd == .true.?"}
    CHECK_CRD_OUT -->|Yes| WRITE_CRD_FILE["Write CRD file<br/>output.f90:302-312"]
    CHECK_CRD_OUT -->|No| DONE
    WRITE_CRD_FILE --> DONE["Output files written"]
    WRITE_XYZ --> DONE
    WRITE_TINKER --> DONE
```

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:146-272](), [src/output.f90:9-539](), [src/input.f90:47-50]()

## PDB Format Output

The PDB (Protein Data Bank) format is the most feature-rich output option, supporting multiple customization options.

### PDB File Structure

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "PDB Output Structure"
        HEADER["HEADER line<br/>output.f90:151-157"]
        REMARK["REMARK lines<br/>output.f90:151-162"]
        CRYST1["CRYST1 (if PBC)<br/>output.f90:164-171"]
        ATOMS["ATOM/HETATM records<br/>output.f90:218-320"]
        TER["TER records (optional)<br/>output.f90:319,425"]
        CONECT["CONECT records<br/>output.f90:429-465"]
        END_REC["END record<br/>output.f90:466"]
    end
    
    HEADER --> REMARK
    REMARK --> CRYST1
    CRYST1 --> ATOMS
    ATOMS --> TER
    TER --> CONECT
    CONECT --> END_REC
```

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:134-469]()

### PDB Output Options

The following table summarizes PDB-specific options that can be set in the input file:

| Keyword | Effect | Default | Code Reference |
|---------|--------|---------|----------------|
| `add_amber_ter` | Add TER records between molecules | `false` | [src/getinp.f90:126-128]() |
| `amber_ter_preserve` | Preserve TER records from input files | `false` | [src/getinp.f90:129-131]() |
| `add_box_sides [value]` | Add CRYST1 record with box dimensions | `false` | [src/getinp.f90:150-158]() |
| `hexadecimal_indices` | Use hexadecimal for atom/residue indices >9999/99999 | `false` | [src/getinp.f90:98-99]() |
| `resnumbers <0\|1\|2\|3>` | Residue numbering scheme (per structure) | Auto-detect | [src/getinp.f90:825-827]() |
| `changechains` | Alternate chain IDs for molecules (per structure) | `false` | [src/getinp.f90:822-824]() |
| `chain <char>` | Force specific chain identifier (per structure) | Auto | [src/getinp.f90:833-835]() |
| `connect <yes\|no>` | Include connectivity (CONECT records) | `yes` | [src/getinp.f90:828-832]() |
| `segid <identifier>` | Set segment identifier for CRD format | Empty | [src/getinp.f90:836-838]() |

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:126-158](), [src/getinp.f90:812-868]()

### Residue Numbering Schemes

Packmol supports four residue numbering schemes controlled by the `resnumbers` keyword within each `structure...end structure` block:

```mermaid
graph TD
    START["Residue Numbering<br/>output.f90:270-284"] --> SCHEME{"resnumbers value"}
    
    SCHEME -->|0| MODE0["Mode 0: By Molecule<br/>iires = mod(imol, 9999)<br/>output.f90:271-272"]
    SCHEME -->|1| MODE1["Mode 1: From Input<br/>iires = imark (from PDB)<br/>output.f90:274-275"]
    SCHEME -->|2| MODE2["Mode 2: Sequential<br/>iires = mod(imark-ifres+irescount, 9999)<br/>output.f90:277-278"]
    SCHEME -->|3| MODE3["Mode 3: Absolute Molecule<br/>iires = mod(iimol, 9999)<br/>output.f90:280-281"]
    
    MODE0 --> HANDLE_ZERO["If iires == 0:<br/>iires = 9999<br/>output.f90:283"]
    MODE1 --> HANDLE_ZERO
    MODE2 --> HANDLE_ZERO
    MODE3 --> HANDLE_ZERO
    
    HANDLE_ZERO --> WRITE_ATOM["Write ATOM/HETATM line<br/>output.f90:287-300"]
```

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:270-284](), [src/getinp.f90:849-857]()

### Atom Index Formatting

When atom or residue indices exceed PDB format limits, Packmol can automatically switch to hexadecimal representation:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Index Formatting Functions"
        I5HEX["i5hex function<br/>output.f90:541-551"]
        I4HEX["i4hex function<br/>output.f90:553-563"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Logic"
        CHECK5["i > 99999 or<br/>hexadecimal_indices?"]
        CHECK4["i > 9999 or<br/>hexadecimal_indices?"]
    end
    
    I5HEX --> CHECK5
    CHECK5 -->|Yes| HEX5["write(i5hex,'(z5)')"]
    CHECK5 -->|No| DEC5["write(i5hex,'(i5)')"]
    
    I4HEX --> CHECK4
    CHECK4 -->|Yes| HEX4["write(i4hex,'(z4)')"]
    CHECK4 -->|No| DEC4["write(i4hex,'(i4)')"]
```

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:541-563](), [src/getinp.f90:98-99]()

### PDB Atom Line Format

The PDB atom line follows the standard PDB format specification with customizable indices:

```
Column  Field        Content
------  -----        -------
1-6     Record type  "ATOM  " or "HETATM"
7-11    Atom serial  Integer (or hex if >99999)
13-16   Atom name    From input PDB
18-21   Residue name From input PDB  
22      Chain ID     From chain/changechains logic
23-26   Residue seq  Integer (or hex if >9999)
27      Insertion    From input PDB
31-38   X coord      Computed position
39-46   Y coord      Computed position
47-54   Z coord      Computed position
55-80   Other fields From input PDB (B-factor, etc.)
```

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:135-137](), [src/output.f90:287-300]()

## Tinker XYZ Format

The Tinker format includes atomic connectivity information required by the Tinker molecular modeling package.

### Tinker Output Structure

```mermaid
graph TD
    START["Write Tinker Output<br/>output.f90:473-536"] --> HEADER["Write header line<br/>natoms + title<br/>output.f90:479"]
    
    HEADER --> INIT["Initialize counters<br/>ilubar, ilugan, icart<br/>output.f90:481-486"]
    
    INIT --> TYPE_LOOP["For each molecule type<br/>output.f90:488"]
    
    TYPE_LOOP --> CHECK_FIXED{"Fixed molecule?"}
    
    CHECK_FIXED -->|No| MOVABLE["Process movable molecules<br/>output.f90:490-516"]
    CHECK_FIXED -->|Yes| FIXED["Process fixed molecules<br/>output.f90:518-531"]
    
    MOVABLE --> TRANSFORM["Transform coordinates<br/>eulerrmat + compcart<br/>output.f90:500-506"]
    FIXED --> WRITE_FIXED["Write fixed coords<br/>output.f90:528"]
    
    TRANSFORM --> ADJ_CONNECT["Adjust connectivity indices<br/>ntcon = nconnect + i_ref_atom<br/>output.f90:508"]
    
    ADJ_CONNECT --> WRITE_LINE["Write Tinker atom line<br/>output.f90:509"]
    WRITE_FIXED --> WRITE_LINE_F["Write Tinker atom line<br/>output.f90:528"]
    
    WRITE_LINE --> TYPE_LOOP
    WRITE_LINE_F --> TYPE_LOOP
    
    TYPE_LOOP -->|Done| CLOSE["Close file<br/>output.f90:535"]
```

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:473-536]()

### Tinker Atom Line Format

Each atom line in Tinker format contains:

```
Field       Content
-----       -------
Atom index  Sequential integer
Element     3-character element symbol
X, Y, Z     Cartesian coordinates (3 x 10.6 format)
Connects    Up to 9 connectivity indices
```

The connectivity indices are adjusted to reflect the absolute atom numbering in the output file using the formula: `ntcon(k) = nconnect(idatom,k) + i_ref_atom`.

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:475](), [src/output.f90:507-509]()

## Standard XYZ Format

The simplest output format, containing only atom types and Cartesian coordinates.

### XYZ Output Process

```mermaid
graph LR
    START["Write XYZ Output<br/>output.f90:93-131"] --> COUNT["Write atom count<br/>output.f90:95"]
    COUNT --> TITLE["Write title line<br/>output.f90:96"]
    TITLE --> LOOP["Loop over molecule types<br/>output.f90:102-128"]
    
    LOOP --> CHECK{"Fixed?"}
    CHECK -->|No| TRANSFORM["Transform coords<br/>eulerrmat + compcart<br/>output.f90:106-116"]
    CHECK -->|Yes| WRITE_FIXED["Write fixed coords<br/>coor(idatom,1:3)<br/>output.f90:126"]
    
    TRANSFORM --> WRITE_MOV["Write movable coords<br/>ele + xcart<br/>output.f90:116"]
    
    WRITE_MOV --> LOOP
    WRITE_FIXED --> LOOP
    LOOP -->|Done| CLOSE["Close file<br/>output.f90:130"]
```

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:93-131]()

### XYZ Line Format

```
Format: element_symbol  x_coord  y_coord  z_coord
Example: C     12.345678    23.456789    34.567890
```

The format string is: `"( tr2,a3,tr2,3(tr2,f14.6) )"` which produces 3-character element symbols followed by three 14.6 floating-point coordinates.

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:116](), [src/output.f90:126]()

## CHARMM CRD Format

The CHARMM CRD format is written as a supplemental output when `writecrd` is specified, always in conjunction with PDB output.

### CRD File Structure

```mermaid
graph TD
    START["CRD Output<br/>output.f90:141-149"] --> HEADER["Write TITLE lines<br/>output.f90:143-147"]
    HEADER --> NATOMS["Write atom count + 'EXT'<br/>output.f90:148"]
    NATOMS --> ATOM_LOOP["Write atom records<br/>output.f90:302-312"]
    
    ATOM_LOOP --> FORMAT_LINE["Format atom line<br/>crd_format string<br/>output.f90:138"]
    
    FORMAT_LINE --> FIELDS["Fields:<br/>atom_id, residue_id<br/>residue_name, atom_name<br/>x, y, z<br/>segid, residue_str<br/>charge"]
    
    FIELDS --> WRITE["Write CRD line<br/>output.f90:309-311"]
```

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:138-149](), [src/output.f90:302-312]()

### CRD Format Specification

The CRD format string is: `'(2I10,2X,A8,2X,A8,3F20.10,2X,A8,2X,A8,F20.10)'`

| Field | Format | Description |
|-------|--------|-------------|
| Atom serial | I10 | Atom index (10 digits) |
| Residue serial | I10 | Residue index (10 digits) |
| Residue name | A8 | 8-character residue name |
| Atom name | A8 | 8-character atom name |
| X, Y, Z | 3F20.10 | Coordinates (20.10 format each) |
| Segment ID | A8 | 8-character segment identifier |
| Residue string | A8 | Residue number as string |
| Charge | F20.10 | Atomic charge (written as 0.0) |

The CRD format supports up to 99,999,999 residues before wrapping (vs. 9,999 for PDB).

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:138](), [src/output.f90:302-312](), [src/getinp.f90:883-886]()

## Connectivity Information

Connectivity (CONECT records in PDB, connectivity indices in Tinker) is read from input files and written to output files.

### Connectivity Writing Process

```mermaid
graph TD
    START["write_connect subroutine<br/>output.f90:565-598"] --> CHECK["Check maxcon(iiat)<br/>output.f90:573"]
    CHECK -->|0| RETURN["Return (no connectivity)<br/>output.f90:573"]
    CHECK -->|>0| INIT["Initialize CONECT line<br/>output.f90:577"]
    
    INIT --> LOOP["Loop over connections<br/>output.f90:578-597"]
    
    LOOP --> ADD_INDEX["Add connection index<br/>i5hex(nconnect+ifirst-1)<br/>output.f90:579"]
    
    ADD_INDEX --> CHECK_FINISH{"Last connection or<br/>line full (5 atoms)?"}
    
    CHECK_FINISH -->|Yes| WRITE_LINE["Write CONECT line<br/>output.f90:583,592"]
    CHECK_FINISH -->|No| CHECK_ORDER{"Next index ><br/>current index?"}
    
    CHECK_ORDER -->|Yes| CONTINUE["Add to same line<br/>output.f90:588"]
    CHECK_ORDER -->|No| NEW_LINE["Start new CONECT line<br/>output.f90:594"]
    
    WRITE_LINE --> LOOP
    CONTINUE --> LOOP
    NEW_LINE --> LOOP
    
    LOOP -->|Done| RETURN_END["Return"]
```

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:565-598]()

### CONECT Record Format

CONECT records follow PDB format specifications:
- Maximum of 4 bonded atoms per line (excluding the central atom)
- Multiple CONECT lines for atoms with >4 bonds
- Indices must be in increasing order
- Uses `i5hex` formatting for hexadecimal support

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:565-598](), [src/output.f90:541-551]()

## Restart Files

Packmol can write restart files containing generalized coordinates (center of mass + Euler angles) for molecular configurations.

### Restart File Structure

```mermaid
graph TD
    START["Write Restart Files<br/>output.f90:46-89"] --> CHECK_ALL{"restart_to(0)<br/>!= 'none'?"}
    
    CHECK_ALL -->|Yes| WRITE_ALL["Write all-system restart<br/>output.f90:48-63"]
    CHECK_ALL -->|No| TYPE_LOOP
    
    WRITE_ALL --> LOOP_ALL["For each molecule:<br/>xcm(1:3), angles(1:3)<br/>output.f90:57-61"]
    LOOP_ALL --> TYPE_LOOP["Check per-type restarts<br/>output.f90:68-89"]
    
    TYPE_LOOP --> CHECK_TYPE{"restart_to(itype)<br/>!= 'none'?"}
    
    CHECK_TYPE -->|Yes| WRITE_TYPE["Write type-specific restart<br/>output.f90:71-84"]
    CHECK_TYPE -->|No| SKIP["Skip to next type<br/>output.f90:85-88"]
    
    WRITE_TYPE --> LOOP_TYPE["For each molecule of type:<br/>xcm(1:3), angles(1:3)<br/>output.f90:78-82"]
    
    LOOP_TYPE --> TYPE_LOOP
    SKIP --> TYPE_LOOP
    TYPE_LOOP -->|Done| MAIN_OUTPUT["Continue to main output"]
```

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:46-89]()

### Restart File Format

Each line in a restart file contains 6 floating-point values in scientific notation:

```
x_cm  y_cm  z_cm  beta  gama  teta
```

Where:
- `x_cm, y_cm, z_cm`: Center of mass coordinates
- `beta, gama, teta`: Euler angles (in radians)

Format string: `"(6(tr1,es23.16))"` - 6 values with 23.16 scientific notation

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:58]()

### Restart File Usage

Restart files are specified per structure or globally:

```
# Global restart files
restart_from <input_file>    # Read initial positions
restart_to <output_file>      # Write final positions

# Per-structure restart files  
structure ...
  restart_from <input_file>   # For this structure type only
  restart_to <output_file>    # For this structure type only
end structure
```

Fixed molecules cannot use restart files, as validated during input processing.

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:889-928](), [app/packmol.f90:153-158]()

## Coordinate Transformation for Output

All movable molecules undergo coordinate transformation from generalized coordinates to Cartesian coordinates before output.

### Transformation Pipeline

```mermaid
graph LR
    GEN["Generalized Coords<br/>x array: xcm + angles"] --> EULER["Euler Rotation Matrix<br/>eulerrmat(beta,gama,teta)<br/>output.f90:110,243"]
    
    EULER --> ROT_MAT["Rotation vectors<br/>v1, v2, v3"]
    
    ROT_MAT --> COMP["Compose Cartesian<br/>compcart(xcart,xcm,coor,v1,v2,v3)<br/>output.f90:115,263"]
    
    COMP --> CART["Cartesian Coords<br/>xcart array"]
    
    subgraph "For Fixed Molecules"
        FIXED_IN["coor array<br/>(from input)"] --> FIXED_OUT["Direct output<br/>No transformation"]
    end
```

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:106-116](), [src/output.f90:239-263]()

### Variable Indexing

The output subroutine uses several index variables to traverse the coordinate arrays:

| Variable | Purpose | Usage |
|----------|---------|-------|
| `ilubar` | Index into center-of-mass positions (`x(1:3*ntotmol)`) | [output.f90:55,97]() |
| `ilugan` | Index into Euler angles (`x(3*ntotmol+1:6*ntotmol)`) | [output.f90:56,98]() |
| `icart` | Index into Cartesian coordinate array `xcart` | [output.f90:99,113]() |
| `idatom` | Index into reference coordinate array `coor` | [output.f90:111,114]() |
| `i_ref_atom` | Running atom counter for output file | [output.f90:176,262]() |

**Sources:** [src/output.f90:55-99](), [src/output.f90:173-177]()

## Output File Name Specification

The output file name is specified using the `output` keyword in the input file:

```
output <filename>
```

The filename is validated during input processing. If missing or incorrectly specified, Packmol exits with an error.

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:258-272]()

### Output Filename Handling

```mermaid
graph TD
    START["Input Processing<br/>getinp.f90:258"] --> INIT["Initialize xyzout = '####'<br/>getinp.f90:260"]
    
    INIT --> SEARCH["Search for 'output' keyword<br/>getinp.f90:261-266"]
    
    SEARCH --> FOUND{"Found output keyword?"}
    
    FOUND -->|Yes| SET["Set xyzout = keyword(iline,2)<br/>getinp.f90:263-264"]
    FOUND -->|No| CHECK
    
    SET --> CHECK{"xyzout == '####'?"}
    
    CHECK -->|Yes| ERROR["ERROR: Output file not specified<br/>getinp.f90:268-270"]
    CHECK -->|No| DISPLAY["Display output filename<br/>getinp.f90:272"]
    
    ERROR --> EXIT["exit_code_input_error"]
    DISPLAY --> CONTINUE["Continue processing"]
```

**Sources:** [src/getinp.f90:258-272]()
