# Page: System Initialization

# System Initialization

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/cli_parser.f90](src/cli_parser.f90)
- [src/initial.f90](src/initial.f90)
- [src/setsizes.f90](src/setsizes.f90)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the system initialization phase implemented in the `initial` subroutine, which prepares the molecular packing problem for optimization. Initialization occurs after input parsing ([4.2](#4.2)) and before the main optimization loop ([4.4](#4.4)). The initialization phase consists of:

- Computing molecular geometry parameters (maximum internal distances)
- Establishing spatial bounds for the system
- Performing constraint satisfaction to ensure all molecules can fit within their specified geometric regions
- Setting up the cell-based spatial partitioning system ([4.5](#4.5))
- Generating random initial positions and orientations for molecules

For information about the constraint evaluation algorithms themselves, see [7.2](#7.2). For the cell indexing and spatial acceleration structures, see [4.5](#4.5).

## Initialization Sequence Overview

The initialization phase executes through several distinct stages, coordinated by the `initial` subroutine in [src/initial.f90:10-557]().

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START["initial(n,x)"] --> INIT_VARS["Initialize Variables<br/>move = false<br/>init1 = false<br/>comptype = true"]
    INIT_VARS --> CALC_DMAX["Calculate dmax(itype)<br/>Maximum internal distance<br/>per molecule type<br/>[56-71]"]
    CALC_DMAX --> CALC_BOUNDS["Calculate Initial Bounds<br/>sizemin, sizemax<br/>±sidemax from origin<br/>[76-85]"]
    CALC_BOUNDS --> RANDOM_GUESS["Generate First Random Guess<br/>x(1:3*ntotmol) = positions<br/>x(3*ntotmol+1:6*ntotmol) = angles<br/>[88-117]"]
    RANDOM_GUESS --> INIT_XCART["Initialize xcart Array<br/>compcart() converts<br/>generalized → Cartesian<br/>[119-165]"]
    INIT_XCART --> CONSTRAINT_PHASE["Constraint Satisfaction Phase<br/>Per-Type Optimization<br/>[167-225]"]
    CONSTRAINT_PHASE --> RESCALE["Rescale Bounds<br/>Based on actual positions<br/>[227-276]"]
    RESCALE --> SETUP_CELLS["Setup Cell Grid<br/>ncells, cell_length<br/>[278-289]"]
    SETUP_CELLS --> ALLOC_CELLS["Allocate Cell Arrays<br/>latomfirst, latomfix<br/>lcellnext, empty_cell<br/>[291-301]"]
    ALLOC_CELLS --> FIXED_MOLS["Add Fixed Molecules<br/>to latomfix arrays<br/>[303-318]"]
    FIXED_MOLS --> RESET_CM["Reset Center of Mass<br/>Compute cm_min, cm_max<br/>[320-337]"]
    RESET_CM --> CHECK_RESTART{"Restart File<br/>Available?"}
    CHECK_RESTART -->|Yes| READ_RESTART["Read restart_from(0)<br/>Return early<br/>[339-359]"]
    CHECK_RESTART -->|No| BUILD_RANDOM["Build Random Initial Point<br/>[361-427]"]
    BUILD_RANDOM --> SET_ANGLES["Set Random Angles<br/>Respecting constraints<br/>[429-458]"]
    SET_ANGLES --> TYPE_RESTART{"Type-Specific<br/>Restart Files?"}
    TYPE_RESTART -->|Yes| READ_TYPE_RESTART["Read restart_from(itype)<br/>[473-510]"]
    TYPE_RESTART -->|No| FINAL_CONSTRAINT["Final Constraint Pass<br/>Per-Type Optimization<br/>[516-550]"]
    READ_TYPE_RESTART --> FINAL_CONSTRAINT
    FINAL_CONSTRAINT --> RETURN["Return"]
    READ_RESTART --> RETURN
```

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:10-557]()

## Key Data Structures

The initialization phase sets up and populates several critical data structures that are used throughout the optimization process.

### Generalized Coordinates Array (x)

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "x Array Structure (size = 6*ntotmol)"
        X_POS["x(1:3*ntotmol)<br/>Center of Mass<br/>Positions<br/>(xcm_1, ycm_1, zcm_1,<br/>xcm_2, ..."]
        X_ANG["x(3*ntotmol+1:6*ntotmol)<br/>Euler Angles<br/>(beta_1, gamma_1, theta_1,<br/>beta_2, ..."]
    end
    
    subgraph "Indexing Variables"
        ILUBAR["ilubar<br/>Position index<br/>= 3*(imol-1)"]
        ILUGAN["ilugan<br/>Angle index<br/>= 3*ntotmol + 3*(imol-1)"]
    end
    
    X_POS --> COMPCART["compcart()<br/>Transforms to Cartesian"]
    X_ANG --> EULERRMAT["eulerrmat()<br/>Creates rotation matrix"]
    ILUBAR -.indexes.-> X_POS
    ILUGAN -.indexes.-> X_ANG
    COMPCART --> XCART["xcart(ntotat,3)<br/>Cartesian coordinates<br/>of all atoms"]
```

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:88-117](), [src/initial.f90:121-139]()

### Spatial Bounds and Cell System

| Array | Dimension | Purpose | Initialized At |
|-------|-----------|---------|----------------|
| `dmax(itype)` | `(ntype)` | Maximum internal distance within each molecule type | [56-71]() |
| `sizemin(3)` | `(3)` | Minimum x,y,z coordinates for system bounds | [79](), [231-265]() |
| `sizemax(3)` | `(3)` | Maximum x,y,z coordinates for system bounds | [80](), [231-265]() |
| `ncells(3)` | `(3)` | Number of cells in x,y,z directions | [282]() |
| `cell_length(3)` | `(3)` | Size of each cell in x,y,z directions | [283]() |
| `latomfirst(i,j,k)` | `(ncells(1), ncells(2), ncells(3))` | First atom index in cell (i,j,k) | [292]() |
| `latomfix(i,j,k)` | `(ncells(1), ncells(2), ncells(3))` | First fixed atom index in cell (i,j,k) | [293]() |
| `latomnext(iatom)` | `(ntotat)` | Next atom index in same cell (linked list) | [300]() |

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:56-71](), [src/initial.f90:76-85](), [src/initial.f90:227-276](), [src/initial.f90:278-318]()

## Two-Pass Constraint Satisfaction Strategy

The initialization phase employs a two-pass strategy for constraint satisfaction, implemented using the `swaptype` mechanism. This ensures molecules can satisfy geometric constraints before considering inter-molecular distances.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START_CONSTRAINT["init1 = true<br/>Enable constraint-only mode"] --> INIT_SWAP["swaptype(n,x,itype,0)<br/>Initialize swap arrays"]
    INIT_SWAP --> LOOP_START{"itype <= ntype?"}
    LOOP_START -->|No| RESTORE["swaptype(n,x,itype,3)<br/>Restore all molecules<br/>init1 = false"]
    RESTORE --> END_PHASE["Exit Constraint Phase"]
    
    LOOP_START -->|Yes| SET_TYPE["swaptype(n,x,itype,1)<br/>Isolate molecule type"]
    SET_TYPE --> COMPUTE_F["computef(n,x,fx)<br/>Evaluate constraints only<br/>(init1 = true)"]
    COMPUTE_F --> CHECK_FREST{"frest > precision?"}
    
    CHECK_FREST -->|No| SAVE_TYPE["swaptype(n,x,itype,2)<br/>Save optimized positions"]
    SAVE_TYPE --> NEXT_TYPE["itype = itype + 1"]
    NEXT_TYPE --> LOOP_START
    
    CHECK_FREST -->|Yes| CHECK_ITER{"i < nloop0_type?"}
    CHECK_ITER -->|No| ERROR["ERROR: Cannot satisfy<br/>constraints for this type<br/>exit_code_failed_to_converge"]
    CHECK_ITER -->|Yes| OPTIMIZE["pgencan(n,x,fx)<br/>Constraint-only optimization"]
    OPTIMIZE --> COMPUTE_F2["computef(n,x,fx)<br/>Re-evaluate"]
    COMPUTE_F2 --> CHECK_AGAIN{"frest > precision?"}
    CHECK_AGAIN -->|No| SAVE_TYPE
    CHECK_AGAIN -->|Yes| MOVEBAD["movebad(n,x,fx,movebadprint)<br/>Fix bad orientations"]
    MOVEBAD --> INCREMENT["i = i + 1"]
    INCREMENT --> CHECK_ITER
```

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:167-225](), [src/initial.f90:516-550]()

### The swaptype Mechanism

The `swaptype` subroutine (defined elsewhere in the codebase) temporarily modifies optimization variables to focus on a single molecule type. The operation modes are:

| Mode | Purpose | Effect |
|------|---------|--------|
| 0 | Initialize | Allocate temporary swap arrays |
| 1 | Focus on type | Set variables for molecules of other types to fixed values; only optimize current type |
| 2 | Save results | Store optimized positions for current type |
| 3 | Restore all | Restore full variable arrays with all molecule types active |

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:175-183](), [src/initial.f90:206](), [src/initial.f90:500-505](), [src/initial.f90:519-548]()

### First Pass: Constraint Satisfaction Without Distances

The first constraint satisfaction pass (lines 167-225) processes each molecule type sequentially:

1. **Isolate Type**: Call `swaptype(n,x,itype,1)` to focus optimization on molecules of type `itype`
2. **Optimize**: Run `pgencan` (GENCAN with projections) with `init1 = .true.`, which causes `computef` to evaluate only constraint violations (`frest`), ignoring inter-molecular distances
3. **Fix Bad Orientations**: If constraints still violated, call `movebad` to reposition molecules that cannot satisfy constraints
4. **Iterate**: Repeat up to `nloop0_type(itype)` times until `frest <= precision`
5. **Save**: Call `swaptype(n,x,itype,2)` to store optimized positions

This pass ensures that each molecule type can individually satisfy its geometric constraints (e.g., inside/outside cube/sphere) before attempting to pack multiple types together.

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:167-225]()

### Second Pass: Final Constraint Adjustment

The second constraint satisfaction pass (lines 516-550) occurs after random position generation and has the same structure but different context:

- Executes only for types without restart files (`restart_from(itype) == 'none'`)
- Uses the randomly generated positions from lines 361-427
- Ensures the random positions also satisfy geometric constraints
- Can also terminate if `randini = .true.` (lines 514), skipping this pass entirely

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:516-550]()

## Cell Grid Initialization

After constraint satisfaction, the system establishes the spatial partitioning grid used for efficient distance calculations during optimization.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input Parameters"
        RADMAX["radmax<br/>Maximum atomic radius"]
        DISCALE["discale<br/>Cell scaling factor<br/>(typically ~1.0)"]
        PBC_LENGTH["pbc_length(3)<br/>System dimensions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Cell Calculation [278-289]"
        CELL_SIDE["cell_side =<br/>discale * 1.01 * radmax"]
        NCELLS["ncells(i) =<br/>max(1, floor(pbc_length(i) / cell_side))"]
        CELL_LENGTH["cell_length(i) =<br/>pbc_length(i) / ncells(i)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Array Allocation [291-296]"
        ALLOC_LATOMFIRST["allocate(latomfirst(ncells(1:3)))"]
        ALLOC_LATOMFIX["allocate(latomfix(ncells(1:3)))"]
        ALLOC_LCELLNEXT["allocate(lcellnext(product(ncells)))"]
        ALLOC_EMPTY["allocate(empty_cell(ncells(1:3)))"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Initialization [297-301]"
        RESET["latomfix = 0<br/>latomfirst = 0<br/>latomnext = 0<br/>empty_cell = true"]
    end
    
    RADMAX --> CELL_SIDE
    DISCALE --> CELL_SIDE
    PBC_LENGTH --> NCELLS
    CELL_SIDE --> NCELLS
    NCELLS --> CELL_LENGTH
    PBC_LENGTH --> CELL_LENGTH
    
    NCELLS --> ALLOC_LATOMFIRST
    NCELLS --> ALLOC_LATOMFIX
    NCELLS --> ALLOC_LCELLNEXT
    NCELLS --> ALLOC_EMPTY
    
    ALLOC_LATOMFIRST --> RESET
    ALLOC_LATOMFIX --> RESET
    ALLOC_LCELLNEXT --> RESET
    ALLOC_EMPTY --> RESET
```

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:278-301]()

### Fixed Molecule Integration

If fixed molecules are present (`fix = .true.`), they are permanently added to the cell indexing structures:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CHECK_FIX{"fix = true?"}
    CHECK_FIX -->|No| SKIP["Skip fixed molecule processing"]
    CHECK_FIX -->|Yes| INIT_ICART["icart = ntotat - nfixedat<br/>Start at first fixed atom"]
    
    INIT_ICART --> LOOP_TYPE["Loop: iftype = ntype+1<br/>to ntype_with_fixed"]
    LOOP_TYPE --> LOOP_ATOM["Loop: ifatom = 1<br/>to natoms(iftype)"]
    LOOP_ATOM --> INCREMENT["icart = icart + 1"]
    INCREMENT --> SETCELL["setcell(xcart(icart,:), cell)<br/>Determine cell indices"]
    SETCELL --> ADD_TO_LATOMNEXT["latomnext(icart) =<br/>latomfix(cell(1:3))"]
    ADD_TO_LATOMNEXT --> UPDATE_LATOMFIX["latomfix(cell(1:3)) = icart"]
    UPDATE_LATOMFIX --> UPDATE_LATOMFIRST["latomfirst(cell(1:3)) = icart"]
    UPDATE_LATOMFIRST --> SET_TYPE_MOL["ibtype(icart) = iftype<br/>ibmol(icart) = 1"]
    SET_TYPE_MOL --> LOOP_ATOM
```

This creates linked lists in the cell structure so that fixed atoms are considered during distance evaluations in the optimization phase.

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:303-318]()

## Random Position Generation

For molecules without restart files, the system generates random initial positions and orientations with several safeguards.

### Center of Mass Position Generation

The random position generation includes overlap avoidance when `avoidoverlap = .true.` and respects constraint satisfaction:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START_RANDOM["For each molecule type"] --> CHECK_RESTART_TYPE{"restart_from(itype)<br/>!= 'none'?"}
    CHECK_RESTART_TYPE -->|Yes| SKIP_TYPE["Skip this type<br/>ilubar += nmols*3"]
    CHECK_RESTART_TYPE -->|No| LOOP_MOL["For each molecule"]
    
    LOOP_MOL --> CHECK_AVOIDOVERLAP{"avoidoverlap = true?"}
    
    CHECK_AVOIDOVERLAP -->|No| SIMPLE_GEN["ntry = 0<br/>fx = 1.0"]
    SIMPLE_GEN --> SIMPLE_LOOP{"fx > precision<br/>AND ntry < max_guess_try?"}
    SIMPLE_LOOP -->|No| NEXT_MOL
    SIMPLE_LOOP -->|Yes| GEN_RANDOM["xrnd = random(0,1)<br/>x(ilubar+1:3) = cm_min + xrnd*(cm_max-cm_min)"]
    GEN_RANDOM --> RESTMOL["restmol(itype, ilubar, n, x, fx, false)<br/>Check constraint satisfaction"]
    RESTMOL --> INC_NTRY["ntry += 1"]
    INC_NTRY --> SIMPLE_LOOP
    
    CHECK_AVOIDOVERLAP -->|Yes| COMPLEX_GEN["ntry = 0<br/>fx = 1.0<br/>overlap = false"]
    COMPLEX_GEN --> COMPLEX_LOOP{"overlap OR fx > precision<br/>AND ntry < max_guess_try?"}
    COMPLEX_LOOP -->|No| NEXT_MOL["ilubar += 3"]
    COMPLEX_LOOP -->|Yes| RESET_OVERLAP["overlap = false<br/>ntry += 1"]
    RESET_OVERLAP --> GEN_RANDOM2["xrnd = random(0,1)<br/>x(ilubar+1:3) = cm_min + xrnd*(cm_max-cm_min)"]
    GEN_RANDOM2 --> CHECK_FIX2{"fix = true?"}
    CHECK_FIX2 -->|No| RESTMOL2["restmol(...)<br/>Check constraints"]
    CHECK_FIX2 -->|Yes| SETCELL2["setcell(x(ilubar+1:3), cell)<br/>Determine cell"]
    SETCELL2 --> CHECK_NEIGHBORS["Check 3x3x3<br/>neighbor cells<br/>for latomfix != 0"]
    CHECK_NEIGHBORS --> SET_OVERLAP{"Found fixed<br/>atom nearby?"}
    SET_OVERLAP -->|Yes| SET_OVERLAP_TRUE["overlap = true"]
    SET_OVERLAP -->|No| RESTMOL2
    SET_OVERLAP_TRUE --> COMPLEX_LOOP
    RESTMOL2 --> COMPLEX_LOOP
    
    NEXT_MOL --> LOOP_MOL
```

**Key Variables:**
- `cm_min(itype,3)`, `cm_max(itype,3)`: Bounds for center of mass positions, computed from actual molecule positions after constraint satisfaction [src/initial.f90:323-337]()
- `max_guess_try`: Maximum attempts to find valid position (20 for normal mode, 1 for gradient checking) [src/initial.f90:367-375]()
- `scale_rnd_guess`: Scaling factor for random generation (1.0 normally, 1.5 for gradient checking) [src/initial.f90:371-374]()

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:378-427]()

### Angle Generation

After positions, random Euler angles are generated for each molecule, respecting any rotation constraints:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START_ANGLES["ilugan = ntotmol*3<br/>Start of angle section"] --> LOOP_TYPE["For each type"]
    LOOP_TYPE --> CHECK_RESTART_ANG{"restart_from(itype)<br/>!= 'none'?"}
    CHECK_RESTART_ANG -->|Yes| SKIP_ANGLES["ilugan += nmols*3"]
    CHECK_RESTART_ANG -->|No| LOOP_MOL_ANG["For each molecule"]
    
    LOOP_MOL_ANG --> ANGLE_BETA["Generate beta (x(ilugan+1))"]
    ANGLE_BETA --> CHECK_BETA{"constrain_rot(itype,1)?"}
    CHECK_BETA -->|Yes| BOUNDED_BETA["x(ilugan+1) = (bound_center - bound_width)<br/>+ 2*rnd()*bound_width"]
    CHECK_BETA -->|No| FREE_BETA["x(ilugan+1) = twopi*rnd()"]
    
    BOUNDED_BETA --> ANGLE_GAMMA["Generate gamma (x(ilugan+2))"]
    FREE_BETA --> ANGLE_GAMMA
    ANGLE_GAMMA --> CHECK_GAMMA{"constrain_rot(itype,2)?"}
    CHECK_GAMMA -->|Yes| BOUNDED_GAMMA["x(ilugan+2) = bounded"]
    CHECK_GAMMA -->|No| FREE_GAMMA["x(ilugan+2) = twopi*rnd()"]
    
    BOUNDED_GAMMA --> ANGLE_THETA["Generate theta (x(ilugan+3))"]
    FREE_GAMMA --> ANGLE_THETA
    ANGLE_THETA --> CHECK_THETA{"constrain_rot(itype,3)?"}
    CHECK_THETA -->|Yes| BOUNDED_THETA["x(ilugan+3) = bounded"]
    CHECK_THETA -->|No| FREE_THETA["x(ilugan+3) = twopi*rnd()"]
    
    BOUNDED_THETA --> NEXT_MOL_ANG["ilugan += 3"]
    FREE_THETA --> NEXT_MOL_ANG
    NEXT_MOL_ANG --> LOOP_MOL_ANG
```

The rotation bounds are specified in the input file via the `constrain_rotation` keyword. If constrained, angles are generated uniformly within the specified bounds; otherwise, they span the full range [0, 2π).

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:429-458]()

## Restart File Handling

The initialization system supports three restart modes, allowing users to resume from previous runs or provide custom initial configurations.

### Restart Hierarchy

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START["Check Restart Options"] --> CHECK_GLOBAL{"restart_from(0)<br/>!= 'none'?"}
    
    CHECK_GLOBAL -->|Yes| READ_GLOBAL["Read Global Restart File<br/>All molecules, all types<br/>[339-359]"]
    READ_GLOBAL --> RETURN_EARLY["Return immediately<br/>Skip all other initialization"]
    
    CHECK_GLOBAL -->|No| CHECK_TYPE_SPECIFIC["After random generation...<br/>Check type-specific restarts"]
    CHECK_TYPE_SPECIFIC --> LOOP_TYPES["For each itype = 1 to ntype"]
    LOOP_TYPES --> CHECK_TYPE_RESTART{"restart_from(itype)<br/>!= 'none'?"}
    
    CHECK_TYPE_RESTART -->|No| SKIP_TYPE_RESTART["Use randomly generated<br/>positions/angles"]
    CHECK_TYPE_RESTART -->|Yes| OPEN_FILE["Open restart_from(itype)<br/>[484]"]
    OPEN_FILE --> READ_MOLS["For i = 1 to nmols(itype)<br/>Read 6 values per molecule<br/>[489-497]"]
    READ_MOLS --> CLOSE_FILE["close(10) [499]"]
    CLOSE_FILE --> SWAP_CHECK["swaptype(n,x,itype,0-1)<br/>Isolate type [500-501]"]
    SWAP_CHECK --> COMPUTE_CHECK["computef(n,x,fx)<br/>Evaluate constraints [502]"]
    COMPUTE_CHECK --> REPORT["Print frest, fdist [503-504]"]
    REPORT --> SWAP_RESTORE["swaptype(n,x,itype,3)<br/>Restore [505]"]
    
    SKIP_TYPE_RESTART --> NEXT_TYPE
    SWAP_RESTORE --> NEXT_TYPE["Next type"]
    NEXT_TYPE --> LOOP_TYPES
```

### Restart File Format

All restart files (global and type-specific) use the same format - one line per molecule with 6 space-separated values:

```
xcm_x  xcm_y  xcm_z  beta  gamma  theta
```

Where:
- `xcm_x, xcm_y, xcm_z`: Center of mass coordinates
- `beta, gamma, theta`: Euler angles (in radians)

**Example:**
```
10.5  20.3  15.7  1.234  2.456  0.789
11.2  19.8  16.1  0.567  1.890  2.345
...
```

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:339-359](), [src/initial.f90:473-510]()

### Restart Validation

Type-specific restart files are validated immediately after reading:

1. The `swaptype` mechanism isolates the restarted type
2. `computef` evaluates constraint violations (`frest`) and minimum distance violations (`fdist`)
3. Results are printed to inform the user about the quality of the restart configuration
4. Variables are restored to include all molecules

This allows users to detect if their restart file contains molecules outside the specified geometric constraints.

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:500-505]()

## Special Modes and Edge Cases

### Gradient Checking Mode

When `chkgrad = .true.` (enabled via input keyword), initialization behavior changes:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CHKGRAD["chkgrad = true"] --> DISABLE_AVOID["avoidoverlap = false<br/>[368-369]"]
    DISABLE_AVOID --> MAX_TRY["max_guess_try = 1<br/>[370]"]
    MAX_TRY --> SCALE_OUT["scale_rnd_guess = 1.5<br/>Place outside constraints<br/>[371]"]
    SCALE_OUT --> COMPARE["comparegrad(n,x)<br/>Compare analytical vs<br/>finite-difference gradients<br/>[468]"]
    COMPARE --> STOP["stop<br/>(Exit after checking)<br/>[469]"]
```

This mode intentionally places molecules outside their constraint regions to verify that gradient calculations correctly identify and penalize constraint violations.

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:367-470]()

### Boundary Condition Handling

The system handles both periodic and non-periodic boundary conditions during initialization:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    RESCALE_DONE["After rescaling sizemin/sizemax<br/>[227-265]"] --> CHECK_PBC{"using_pbc?"}
    
    CHECK_PBC -->|Yes| KEEP_PBC["Keep user-specified<br/>pbc_min, pbc_max, pbc_length<br/>(set during input parsing)"]
    
    CHECK_PBC -->|No| SET_PSEUDO_PBC["pbc_min = sizemin<br/>pbc_max = sizemax<br/>pbc_length = pbc_max - pbc_min<br/>[272-276]"]
    
    SET_PSEUDO_PBC --> EXPLAIN["System uses PBCs internally<br/>but with extra cell layer<br/>to prevent cross-boundary interactions"]
    
    KEEP_PBC --> CELL_CALC["Calculate cell grid<br/>based on pbc_length<br/>[278-289]"]
    EXPLAIN --> CELL_CALC
```

When periodic boundaries are not explicitly specified, the system creates "pseudo-PBCs" sized to the actual molecular distribution plus padding (`1.1 * radmax`). This allows the cell indexing system to work uniformly, but prevents molecules from interacting across the boundaries due to an empty cell layer.

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:266-276]()

### Fixed Molecule Validation

For fixed molecules, the system validates that all atoms lie within the specified periodic boundary box:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PROCESS_FIXED["Processing fixed molecules<br/>[140-165]"] --> LOOP_FIXED["For each fixed atom"]
    LOOP_FIXED --> CALC_POS["xcart(icart,1:3) = coor(idfatom,1:3)<br/>Copy coordinates"]
    CALC_POS --> SET_FIXED["fixedatom(icart) = true"]
    SET_FIXED --> CHECK_PBC_FIX{"using_pbc?"}
    
    CHECK_PBC_FIX -->|No| NEXT_ATOM["Next atom"]
    CHECK_PBC_FIX -->|Yes| LOOP_COORD["For i = 1 to 3"]
    LOOP_COORD --> CHECK_BOUNDS{"xcart(icart,i) in<br/>[pbc_min(i), pbc_max(i)]?"}
    
    CHECK_BOUNDS -->|Yes| NEXT_COORD["Next coordinate"]
    CHECK_BOUNDS -->|No| ERROR["ERROR: Fixed molecule<br/>outside PBC box<br/>exit_code_input_error<br/>[155-160]"]
    
    NEXT_COORD --> LOOP_COORD
    LOOP_COORD -->|Done| NEXT_ATOM
```

This validation prevents silent failures where fixed molecules would be invisible to the optimization because they're outside the cell grid.

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:152-162]()

## Performance Considerations

### Cell Size Selection

The cell grid size is critical for optimization performance. The cell side length is set to:

```
cell_side = discale * 1.01 * radmax
```

Where:
- `radmax`: Maximum atomic radius across all atom types
- `discale`: User-specified scaling factor (default ~1.0, can be adjusted via `discale` keyword)
- Factor 1.01: Small safety margin

This ensures that atoms can only interact with atoms in their own cell and the 26 neighboring cells (3×3×3 - 1 = 26 forward neighbors when avoiding double-counting). Larger cells reduce memory but increase the number of distance calculations per cell; smaller cells do the opposite.

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:280]()

### Constraint Satisfaction Iteration Limits

Each molecule type has a per-type iteration limit `nloop0_type(itype)` for the constraint satisfaction phase (default value set in `setsizes`, can be overridden via `nloop0` keyword in input). If constraints cannot be satisfied within this limit, the program terminates with an error message suggesting:

1. The geometric constraints may be impossible to satisfy
2. Try increasing `nloop0` value (e.g., `nloop0 1000`)

**Sources:** [src/initial.f90:191](), [src/initial.f90:218-222]()

# Page: Optimization Engine (GENCAN)

# Optimization Engine (GENCAN)

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/ahestetic.f90](src/ahestetic.f90)
- [src/gencan.f](src/gencan.f)
- [src/gencan_ieee_signal_routines.f90](src/gencan_ieee_signal_routines.f90)
- [src/heuristics.f90](src/heuristics.f90)
- [src/initial.f90](src/initial.f90)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the GENCAN optimization solver and its integration into Packmol. GENCAN is a bound-constrained optimization algorithm that forms the core numerical engine for solving the molecular packing problem. For details on how the objective function and gradient are computed, see [Objective Function Evaluation](#4.6). For the overall program execution flow, see [Program Execution Flow](#4.2). For the initialization phase that uses GENCAN, see [System Initialization](#4.3).

## Overview

GENCAN (GENeralized projected gradient method for box-Constrained problems) is a large-scale active-set optimization method that combines:
- **Spectral Projected Gradient (SPG)** for first-order search directions
- **Truncated Newton** for second-order acceleration
- **Active-set strategy** for handling bound constraints efficiently

The solver is implemented in Fortran 77 in [src/gencan.f]() and is accessed through wrapper functions in [src/pgencan.f90](). The method is described in the paper by E. G. Birgin and J. M. Martinez (2002) referenced in [src/gencan.f:786-791]().

Sources: [src/gencan.f:1-3000](), [src/pgencan.f90:1-100]()

## Integration Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Packmol High-Level Loop"
        INITIAL["initial.f90<br/>Constraint Satisfaction"]
        MAIN_LOOP["Main Optimization Loop<br/>app/packmol.f90"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Packmol-GENCAN Interface Layer"
        PGENCAN["pgencan<br/>Fortran 90 wrapper"]
        EASYGENCAN["easygencan<br/>Simplified GENCAN caller"]
    end
    
    subgraph "GENCAN Core (src/gencan.f)"
        GENCAN_MAIN["gencan<br/>Main optimization routine"]
        SPG["Spectral Projected<br/>Gradient iteration"]
        TN["Truncated Newton<br/>iteration"]
        CG["Conjugate Gradients<br/>solver"]
    end
    
    subgraph "User-Supplied Functions"
        EVALAL["evalal<br/>Objective function"]
        EVALNAL["evalnal<br/>Gradient"]
        EVALHD["evalhd<br/>Hessian-vector product"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Packmol Function Evaluation"
        COMPUTEF["computef.f90<br/>Calculate f(x)"]
        COMPUTEG["computeg.f90<br/>Calculate ∇f(x)"]
    end
    
    INITIAL --> PGENCAN
    MAIN_LOOP --> PGENCAN
    PGENCAN --> EASYGENCAN
    EASYGENCAN --> GENCAN_MAIN
    
    GENCAN_MAIN --> SPG
    GENCAN_MAIN --> TN
    TN --> CG
    
    SPG --> EVALAL
    SPG --> EVALNAL
    TN --> EVALNAL
    TN --> EVALHD
    
    EVALAL --> COMPUTEF
    EVALNAL --> COMPUTEG
    EVALHD -.-> |"not used<br/>(approx by quotients)"| COMPUTEG
    
    COMPUTEF -.-> |"returns f"| EVALAL
    COMPUTEG -.-> |"returns g"| EVALNAL
```

**Diagram: GENCAN integration architecture showing call flow from Packmol to GENCAN core**

Sources: [src/initial.f90:194-200](), [src/gencan.f:202-739](), [src/pgencan.f90:1-100]()

## Interface Functions

GENCAN requires three user-supplied subroutines that connect it to the specific problem being solved. In Packmol, these are implemented as thin wrappers around the core function evaluation routines.

### evalal: Objective Function Evaluation

```mermaid
graph LR
    GENCAN["GENCAN core"] --> EVALAL["evalal(n,x,m,lambda,rho,f,flag)"]
    EVALAL --> COMPUTEF["computef(n,x,f)"]
    COMPUTEF --> DISTANCE["Distance penalties<br/>fparc.f90"]
    COMPUTEF --> CONSTRAINT["Constraint penalties<br/>comprest.f90"]
    DISTANCE --> F["f: objective value"]
    CONSTRAINT --> F
    F --> EVALAL
    EVALAL --> GENCAN
```

**Diagram: evalal function connects GENCAN to Packmol's objective function**

The `evalal` subroutine is defined in [src/gencan.f:4-57]() and serves as the callback that GENCAN uses to evaluate the objective function. The implementation simply calls `computef`:

```fortran
subroutine evalal(n,x,m,lambda,rho,f,flag)
    flag = 0
    call computef(n,x,f)
end
```

**Parameters:**
- `n`: Number of variables (3 × number of molecules for positions, +3 × number of molecules for orientations)
- `x(n)`: Current point (generalized coordinates)
- `m, lambda(m), rho(m)`: Augmented Lagrangian parameters (unused in Packmol; kept for interface compatibility)
- `f`: Returned objective function value
- `flag`: Error indicator (0 = success)

Sources: [src/gencan.f:4-57](), [src/computef.f90:1-100]()

### evalnal: Gradient Evaluation

```mermaid
graph LR
    GENCAN["GENCAN core"] --> EVALNAL["evalnal(n,x,m,lambda,rho,g,flag)"]
    EVALNAL --> COMPUTEG["computeg(n,x,g)"]
    COMPUTEG --> GRAD_DIST["Distance gradients<br/>gparc.f90"]
    COMPUTEG --> GRAD_CONST["Constraint gradients<br/>gwalls.f90"]
    GRAD_DIST --> G["g: gradient vector"]
    GRAD_CONST --> G
    G --> EVALNAL
    EVALNAL --> GENCAN
```

**Diagram: evalnal function connects GENCAN to Packmol's gradient computation**

The `evalnal` subroutine is defined in [src/gencan.f:62-115]() and provides gradient information:

```fortran
subroutine evalnal(n,x,m,lambda,rho,g,flag)
    flag = 0
    call computeg(n,x,g)
end
```

**Parameters:**
- `g(n)`: Returned gradient vector ∇f(x)
- Other parameters same as `evalal`

Sources: [src/gencan.f:62-115](), [src/computeg.f90:1-200]()

### evalhd: Hessian-Vector Product

The `evalhd` subroutine [src/gencan.f:125-196]() is implemented as an empty stub in Packmol because GENCAN is configured to approximate Hessian-vector products using incremental quotients (`htvtype = 1` in [src/gencan.f:609]()). This avoids the need to compute or store the full Hessian matrix, which would be prohibitively expensive for large systems.

Sources: [src/gencan.f:125-196](), [src/gencan.f:609]()

## GENCAN Algorithm Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    START["gencan entry"] --> INIT["Initialize parameters<br/>Set bounds l, u"]
    INIT --> EVAL_INITIAL["Evaluate f(x₀), ∇f(x₀)"]
    EVAL_INITIAL --> MAIN_LOOP{"Convergence?<br/>||∇Pf|| < ε"}
    
    MAIN_LOOP -->|No| FACE_CHECK{"Leave<br/>current face?"}
    FACE_CHECK -->|Yes| SPG_ITER["SPG Iteration<br/>First-order direction"]
    FACE_CHECK -->|No| TN_ITER["Truncated Newton<br/>Second-order direction"]
    
    SPG_ITER --> SPG_LS["Line search with<br/>nonmonotone criterion"]
    SPG_LS --> UPDATE_SPECTRAL["Update spectral<br/>steplength λₖ"]
    UPDATE_SPECTRAL --> PROJECTION["Project onto bounds<br/>x ← P[x - λₖ∇f]"]
    
    TN_ITER --> CG_SOLVE["Conjugate Gradients<br/>Solve H d = -∇f"]
    CG_SOLVE --> TN_LS["Line search along d"]
    
    PROJECTION --> EVAL["Evaluate f, ∇f<br/>at new point"]
    TN_LS --> EVAL
    EVAL --> MAIN_LOOP
    
    MAIN_LOOP -->|Yes| RETURN["Return solution"]
    
    style SPG_ITER fill:#f9f9f9
    style TN_ITER fill:#f9f9f9
    style CG_SOLVE fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Diagram: GENCAN main algorithm flow showing SPG and Truncated Newton phases**

### Key Algorithm Components

**Active-Set Strategy**: GENCAN maintains an active set of variables at their bounds. When the projected gradient within the current face is sufficiently small, the algorithm switches to Truncated Newton to accelerate convergence. The parameter `eta` controls this switching [src/gencan.f:476]().

**Spectral Projected Gradient**: Uses a spectral steplength computed from:
```
λₖ = (sₖᵀyₖ) / (yₖᵀyₖ)
```
where `sₖ = xₖ - xₖ₋₁` and `yₖ = ∇f(xₖ) - ∇f(xₖ₋₁)`. The steplength is safeguarded to lie in `[lspgmi, lspgma]` [src/gencan.f:477-478]().

**Nonmonotone Line Search**: Accepts steps that satisfy the Armijo condition with respect to the maximum of the last `p` function values rather than just the previous value. This allows temporary increases in function value to escape narrow valleys.

**Truncated Newton Direction**: Computed by approximately solving the Newton system `H d = -∇f` using Conjugate Gradients within a trust region. The trust region can use Euclidean norm (`trtype=0`) or sup-norm (`trtype=1`).

Sources: [src/gencan.f:750-2000](), [src/gencan.f:429-478]()

## Configuration and Parameters

GENCAN is configured through the `easygencan` wrapper [src/gencan.f:202-739]() which sets most parameters to sensible defaults. Key parameters are:

| Parameter | Default | Description | Source |
|-----------|---------|-------------|--------|
| `epsgpsn` | `precision` | Stopping tolerance for sup-norm of projected gradient | [src/gencan.f:304]() |
| `maxit` | Varies by phase | Maximum number of iterations | [src/gencan.f:307]() |
| `maxfc` | Varies | Maximum number of function evaluations | [src/gencan.f:311]() |
| `gtype` | 0 | Gradient type: 0=user-supplied, 1=finite differences | [src/gencan.f:569]() |
| `htvtype` | 1 | Hessian-vector: 0=user-supplied, 1=incremental quotients | [src/gencan.f:609]() |
| `trtype` | 1 | Trust region type: 0=Euclidean, 1=sup-norm | [src/gencan.f:667]() |
| `eta` | 0.9 | Face-leaving parameter | [src/gencan.f:476]() |
| `gamma` | 1.0e-4 | Armijo condition constant | [src/gencan.f:431]() |
| `delmin` | varies | Minimum trust region radius | [src/gencan.f:659]() |

### Packmol-Specific Parameter Settings

In the initialization phase [src/initial.f90:194](), GENCAN is called with:
- `init1 = .true.` flag set to optimize only constraint violations
- Separate optimization for each molecule type using `swaptype`
- Maximum iterations controlled by `nloop0_type(itype)`

In the main optimization loop, different convergence criteria apply based on whether constraints are satisfied (`frest < precision`) or distance penalties dominate (`fdist`).

Sources: [src/gencan.f:202-739](), [src/initial.f90:168-225]()

## Usage Patterns in Packmol

### Constraint Satisfaction Phase

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Initial as initial.f90
    participant SwapType as swaptype
    participant PGencan as pgencan
    participant Gencan as GENCAN
    participant MoveBad as movebad
    
    Initial->>SwapType: Initialize swap arrays
    loop For each molecule type
        Initial->>SwapType: Set arrays for type i
        loop Until constraints satisfied
            Initial->>PGencan: Optimize constraints only
            PGencan->>Gencan: Call with init1=true
            Gencan-->>PGencan: Return optimized x
            alt frest > precision
                Initial->>MoveBad: Fix bad orientations
                MoveBad-->>Initial: Relocated molecules
            end
        end
        Initial->>SwapType: Save results for type i
    end
    Initial->>SwapType: Restore all-molecule arrays
```

**Diagram: Sequence of GENCAN calls during initialization constraint satisfaction**

During initialization [src/initial.f90:168-225](), GENCAN is used to satisfy geometric constraints for each molecule type independently:

1. **Type-by-type optimization**: The `swaptype` mechanism isolates variables for one molecule type
2. **Constraint-only objective**: With `init1 = .true.`, only constraint penalties contribute to the objective
3. **Iterative refinement**: GENCAN alternates with the `movebad` heuristic to escape local minima
4. **Convergence criterion**: Loop continues until `frest < precision` or maximum iterations reached

Sources: [src/initial.f90:168-225](), [src/swaptype.f90:1-100]()

### Main Optimization Phase

In the main loop [app/packmol.f90:200-400](), GENCAN optimizes the full objective function including both distance penalties and constraint violations:

```fortran
! Main optimization loop
do while (.not. converged)
    call pgencan(n, x, fx)
    call computef(n, x, fx)
    
    if (fdist > precision .or. frest > precision) then
        call movebad(n, x, fx, .true.)
    end if
    
    ! Check convergence
    converged = (fdist < precision .and. frest < precision)
end do
```

**Key differences from initialization:**
- `init1 = .false.` so all penalty terms are active
- All molecule types optimized simultaneously
- Tighter convergence tolerances
- Periodic checkpoint writing if convergence is slow

Sources: [app/packmol.f90:200-400](), [src/computef.f90:1-100]()

## Heuristic Integration

GENCAN is integrated with the `movebad` heuristic [src/heuristics.f90:9-149]() that helps escape local minima:

```mermaid
graph TB
    GENCAN["GENCAN iteration"] --> EVAL["Evaluate f, ∇f"]
    EVAL --> CHECK{"Bad molecules<br/>detected?"}
    CHECK -->|Yes| MOVEBAD["movebad:<br/>Relocate worst molecules"]
    CHECK -->|No| CONTINUE["Continue optimization"]
    MOVEBAD --> SORT["Sort molecules by<br/>penalty contribution"]
    SORT --> RELOCATE["Move worst fraction<br/>to new positions"]
    RELOCATE --> GENCAN
    CONTINUE --> GENCAN
```

**Diagram: Integration of movebad heuristic with GENCAN optimization**

The `movebad` routine:
1. Computes per-molecule penalty contributions using `fdist_atom` and `frest_atom`
2. Sorts molecules by total penalty using flashsort [src/heuristics.f90:92]()
3. Relocates the worst `movefrac` fraction (or up to `maxmove` molecules)
4. New positions are either:
   - Random within size bounds if `movebadrandom = true` [src/heuristics.f90:120-122]()
   - Near good molecules if `movebadrandom = false` [src/heuristics.f90:124-126]()

This provides a global search component that complements GENCAN's local optimization.

Sources: [src/heuristics.f90:9-149](), [src/flashsort.f90:1-100]()

## Conjugate Gradients Tuning

GENCAN's Truncated Newton method uses Conjugate Gradients to solve the Newton system. Several helper routines in [src/gencan_ieee_signal_routines.f90]() adjust CG parameters adaptively:

### Adaptive Accuracy

The `gp_ieee_signal1` routine [src/gencan_ieee_signal_routines.f90:1-11]() computes parameters for logarithmic interpolation of CG accuracy between initial and final tolerances:

```fortran
acgeps = log10(cgepsf / cgepsi) / log10(cggpnf / gpsupn)
bcgeps = log10(cgepsi) - acgeps * log10(gpsupn)
```

This ensures tighter CG convergence as the optimization progresses toward the solution.

### Adaptive Iteration Limit

The `gp_ieee_signal2` routine [src/gencan_ieee_signal_routines.f90:13-45]() dynamically sets `cgmaxit` based on problem dimension and progress:

```fortran
kappa = log10(gpsupn / gpsupn0) / log10(epsgpsn / gpsupn0)
cgmaxit = int((1.0 - kappa) * max(1.0, 10.0 * log10(n)) + kappa * n)
cgmaxit = min(20, cgmaxit)  ! L. Martinez modification
```

The `min(20, cgmaxit)` modification [src/gencan_ieee_signal_routines.f90:34]() was added specifically for Packmol to accelerate iterations near the solution.

Sources: [src/gencan_ieee_signal_routines.f90:1-45](), [src/gencan.f:695-711]()

## Performance Characteristics

| Aspect | Characteristic | Implication |
|--------|---------------|-------------|
| **Scalability** | O(n) per iteration (with sparse Hessian approx) | Handles large systems efficiently |
| **Memory** | O(n) working space | Modest memory requirements |
| **Convergence** | Superlinear near solution (Truncated Newton) | Fast final convergence |
| **Robustness** | Global convergence via SPG | Handles difficult landscapes |
| **Function evaluations** | Typically 5-10 per iteration | Dominated by `computef` cost |

The bottleneck in Packmol is usually the objective function evaluation (distance calculations) rather than the optimization algorithm itself, since GENCAN's computational cost per iteration is negligible compared to O(N) or O(N²) distance calculations.

Sources: [src/gencan.f:786-791](), [src/computef.f90:1-500]()

## Error Handling

GENCAN returns an `inform` code indicating the termination condition:

| inform | Meaning | Action |
|--------|---------|--------|
| 0 | Converged (Euclidean norm criterion) | Success |
| 1 | Converged (sup-norm criterion) | Success |
| 2 | Maximum iterations reached | May need more iterations |
| 3 | Maximum function evaluations reached | Increase `maxfc` |
| 4-6 | Other stopping criteria | Check intermediate output |
| <0 | Error in objective/gradient evaluation | Check `flag` in evalal/evalnal |

In Packmol, if GENCAN fails to converge during initialization, an error message is printed [src/initial.f90:209-222]() suggesting:
- Check spatial constraints for feasibility
- Increase `nloop0` parameter
- Verify molecule geometries

Sources: [src/gencan.f:368-379](), [src/initial.f90:208-223]()

# Spatial Management System

<details>

- [testing/input_files/water_box.inp](testing/input_files/water_box.inp)
- [testing/input_files/water_box_pbc.inp](testing/input_files/water_box_pbc.inp)

## Purpose and Scope

The Spatial Management System in Packmol provides efficient O(N) scaling for pairwise atom interactions through cell-based spatial partitioning. This system divides 3D space into a regular grid of cells and maintains linked-list data structures that enable rapid neighbor searches without evaluating all N² atom pairs.

This document covers the cell indexing algorithms, linked-list structures, and periodic boundary condition (PBC) handling. For information about how these spatial queries are used in distance calculations, see [Atom-to-Atom Interactions](#4.7). For details on the coordinate transformation systems used before spatial indexing, see [Coordinate Transformations](#4.8).

**Sources:** [src/computef.f90:1-154](), [src/computeg.f90:1-246](), [src/cell_indexing.f90:1-63]()

## Overview: Spatial Acceleration Architecture

The spatial management system consists of three interconnected layers: spatial partitioning (cell grid), indexing functions (coordinate-to-cell mapping), and linked-list traversal structures. These components work together to reduce pairwise interaction complexity from O(N²) to O(N).

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Layer 1: Spatial Partitioning"
        BOUNDS["pbc_min, pbc_max<br/>Spatial bounds"]
        GRID["ncells(3)<br/>Cell grid dimensions"]
        LENGTH["cell_length(3)<br/>Cell size"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Layer 2: Cell Indexing"
        SETCELL["setcell(x, cell)<br/>Cartesian → cell(i,j,k)"]
        INDEX["index_cell(cell, ncells)<br/>cell(i,j,k) → linear index"]
        ICELL["icell_to_cell(icell, ncells, cell)<br/>linear index → cell(i,j,k)"]
        CELLIND["cell_ind(icell, ncells)<br/>PBC wrapping"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Layer 3: Linked Lists"
        ALIST["latomfirst(i,j,k)<br/>First atom in cell"]
        ANEXT["latomnext(icart)<br/>Next atom"]
        CLIST["lcellfirst<br/>First occupied cell"]
        CNEXT["lcellnext(icell)<br/>Next occupied cell"]
        EMPTY["empty_cell(i,j,k)<br/>Cell occupancy flag"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Usage in Optimization"
        COMPUTEF["computef.f90<br/>Objective evaluation"]
        COMPUTEG["computeg.f90<br/>Gradient evaluation"]
        NEIGHBOR["14-cell neighbor<br/>search pattern"]
    end
    
    BOUNDS --> LENGTH
    GRID --> LENGTH
    LENGTH --> SETCELL
    
    SETCELL --> ALIST
    SETCELL --> INDEX
    INDEX --> CLIST
    CELLIND --> NEIGHBOR
    
    ALIST --> ANEXT
    CLIST --> CNEXT
    EMPTY --> CLIST
    
    CLIST --> COMPUTEF
    CLIST --> COMPUTEG
    ALIST --> NEIGHBOR
    NEIGHBOR --> COMPUTEF
    NEIGHBOR --> COMPUTEG
    
    style SETCELL fill:#f9f9f9
    style ALIST fill:#f9f9f9
    style CLIST fill:#f9f9f9
    style NEIGHBOR fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [src/cell_indexing.f90:1-63](), [src/computef.f90:1-154](), [src/computeg.f90:1-246](), [src/pbc.f90:1-32]()

## Cell Grid Structure

### Spatial Bounds and Grid Dimensions

The cell grid is defined by spatial bounds (`pbc_min`, `pbc_max`) and cell dimensions (`ncells`). The cell size (`cell_length`) is determined by the interaction cutoff distance to ensure that atoms only interact with those in neighboring cells.

| Variable | Type | Module | Purpose |
|----------|------|--------|---------|
| `pbc_min(3)` | `double precision` | `pbc` | Minimum coordinates of bounding box |
| `pbc_max(3)` | `double precision` | `pbc` | Maximum coordinates of bounding box |
| `pbc_length(3)` | `double precision` | `pbc` | Box dimensions (max - min) |
| `ncells(3)` | `integer` | `compute_data` | Number of cells in each dimension |
| `cell_length(3)` | `double precision` | `compute_data` | Size of each cell |

The cell grid partitions space so that `cell_length ≈ interaction_cutoff`, ensuring that atoms only need to check neighboring cells for potential interactions.

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:1-32](), [src/computef.f90:1-154]()

### Cell Coordinate System

Each cell is identified by 3D indices `cell(1)`, `cell(2)`, `cell(3)` corresponding to i, j, k positions in the grid. The grid satisfies:

```
1 ≤ cell(1) ≤ ncells(1)
1 ≤ cell(2) ≤ ncells(2)
1 ≤ cell(3) ≤ ncells(3)
```

**Sources:** [src/cell_indexing.f90:14-25]()

## Cell Indexing Functions

### setcell: Cartesian to Cell Coordinates

The `setcell` subroutine maps Cartesian coordinates to 3D cell indices. It handles periodic boundary conditions by wrapping coordinates into the simulation box before computing cell indices.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    INPUT["x(3)<br/>Cartesian coordinates"]
    WRAP["xt = v_in_box(x, pbc_min, pbc_length)<br/>Wrap into box"]
    FLOOR["cell = floor((xt - pbc_min) / cell_length) + 1<br/>Compute cell indices"]
    GUARD["cell = min(cell, ncells)<br/>Safeguard for boundary"]
    OUTPUT["cell(3)<br/>Cell indices (i,j,k)"]
    
    INPUT --> WRAP
    WRAP --> FLOOR
    FLOOR --> GUARD
    GUARD --> OUTPUT
```

**Implementation:** [src/cell_indexing.f90:14-25]()

```fortran
subroutine setcell(x,cell)
   xt = v_in_box(x, pbc_min, pbc_length)
   cell(:) = floor((xt(:) - pbc_min(:))/cell_length(:)) + 1
   cell(:) = min(cell(:), ncells(:))
end subroutine setcell
```

**Sources:** [src/cell_indexing.f90:14-25]()

### index_cell: 3D to Linear Indexing

The `index_cell` function converts 3D cell coordinates to a linear index for array storage. This enables efficient cell lookup using a single integer index.

**Mapping Formula:**
```
index_cell = (cell(1)-1) * ncells(2) * ncells(3) 
           + (cell(2)-1) * ncells(3) 
           + (cell(3)-1) + 1
```

This row-major ordering stores cells sequentially: all k values for fixed (i,j), then all j values for fixed i, then all i values.

**Implementation:** [src/cell_indexing.f90:57-60]()

**Sources:** [src/cell_indexing.f90:57-60]()

### icell_to_cell: Linear to 3D Indexing

The inverse operation `icell_to_cell` converts a linear index back to 3D cell coordinates. This is used when iterating through the occupied cell linked list.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    INPUT["icell<br/>Linear index"]
    Z["cell(3) = modulo(icell, ncells(3))<br/>Extract k coordinate"]
    REDUCE1["iicell = (icell - cell(3)) / ncells(3) + 1"]
    Y["cell(2) = modulo(iicell, ncells(2))<br/>Extract j coordinate"]
    REDUCE2["iicell = (iicell - cell(2)) / ncells(2) + 1"]
    X["cell(1) = modulo(iicell, ncells(1))<br/>Extract i coordinate"]
    OUTPUT["cell(3)<br/>Cell indices (i,j,k)"]
    
    INPUT --> Z
    Z --> REDUCE1
    REDUCE1 --> Y
    Y --> REDUCE2
    REDUCE2 --> X
    X --> OUTPUT
```

**Implementation:** [src/cell_indexing.f90:37-55]()

**Sources:** [src/cell_indexing.f90:37-55]()

### cell_ind: PBC Cell Index Wrapping

The `cell_ind` function wraps cell indices for periodic boundary conditions, ensuring indices remain within valid bounds:

```fortran
integer function cell_ind(icell, ncells)
   cell_ind = modulo(icell - 1 + ncells, ncells) + 1
end function cell_ind
```

This is used when accessing neighboring cells that may wrap around box boundaries (e.g., `cell_ind(i+1, ncells(1))` wraps from the last cell to the first).

**Implementation:** [src/pbc.f90:26-29]()

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:26-29]()

## Linked List Data Structures

The spatial management system uses four linked-list arrays to enable efficient traversal of atoms and cells:

### Atom Linked Lists

| Array | Type | Dimensions | Purpose |
|-------|------|------------|---------|
| `latomfirst(i,j,k)` | `integer` | `(ncells(1), ncells(2), ncells(3))` | Index of first atom in cell (i,j,k) |
| `latomnext(icart)` | `integer` | `(ntotat)` | Index of next atom in same cell |

These form a singly-linked list for each cell. Starting from `latomfirst(i,j,k)`, follow `latomnext` pointers until reaching 0 (end of list).

**Example traversal pattern:**
```fortran
icart = latomfirst(i,j,k)
do while( icart > 0 )
   ! Process atom icart
   icart = latomnext(icart)
end do
```

**Sources:** [src/computef.f90:82-88](), [src/computeg.f90:74-78]()

### Cell Linked Lists

| Array | Type | Dimensions | Purpose |
|-------|------|------------|---------|
| `lcellfirst` | `integer` | scalar | Linear index of first occupied cell |
| `lcellnext(icell)` | `integer` | `(ncells(1)*ncells(2)*ncells(3))` | Linear index of next occupied cell |
| `empty_cell(i,j,k)` | `logical` | `(ncells(1), ncells(2), ncells(3))` | Cell occupancy flag |

These form a linked list of only occupied cells, avoiding iteration through empty cells (which is critical when the simulation box is large but sparsely populated).

**Example traversal pattern:**
```fortran
icell = lcellfirst
do while( icell > 0 )
   call icell_to_cell(icell, ncells, cell)
   ! Process cell at cell(1), cell(2), cell(3)
   icell = lcellnext(icell)
end do
```

**Sources:** [src/computef.f90:115-151](), [src/computeg.f90:105-142]()

## Linked List Construction

The linked lists are constructed during objective function and gradient evaluation. The construction happens in both `computef.f90` and `computeg.f90` with identical logic:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    START["Start with atom icart<br/>at position xcart(icart,:)"]
    SETCELL["call setcell(xcart(icart,:), cell)<br/>Determine cell indices"]
    ATOM_LIST["latomnext(icart) = latomfirst(cell)<br/>latomfirst(cell) = icart<br/>Push atom onto cell's list"]
    CHECK["if (empty_cell(cell))"]
    INDEX["icell = index_cell(cell, ncells)<br/>Convert to linear index"]
    CELL_LIST["lcellnext(icell) = lcellfirst<br/>lcellfirst = icell<br/>Push cell onto occupied list"]
    MARK["empty_cell(cell) = .false.<br/>Mark cell as occupied"]
    NEXT["Continue to next atom"]
    
    START --> SETCELL
    SETCELL --> ATOM_LIST
    ATOM_LIST --> CHECK
    CHECK -->|"True"| INDEX
    CHECK -->|"False"| NEXT
    INDEX --> CELL_LIST
    CELL_LIST --> MARK
    MARK --> NEXT
```

**Implementation:** [src/computef.f90:83-101](), [src/computeg.f90:74-90]()

**Sources:** [src/computef.f90:83-101](), [src/computeg.f90:74-90]()

## Neighbor Search Algorithm

### 14-Cell Stencil Pattern

To compute pairwise interactions, each atom queries its own cell and 13 neighboring cells in the "forward" direction. This avoids double-counting pairs (atom A checking atom B's cell is equivalent to atom B checking atom A's cell).

The 14 cells consist of:
1. **Self cell** (1 cell)
2. **Face neighbors** (3 forward: +x, +y, +z)
3. **Edge neighbors** (6 forward: combinations of ±1 in two dimensions, +1 in third)
4. **Vertex neighbors** (4 forward: all combinations of +1 and ±1 in three dimensions)

**Neighbor Cell Access Pattern:**

| Category | Offset (Δi, Δj, Δk) | Cell Access in Code |
|----------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Self | (0, 0, 0) | `latomnext(icart)` |
| Faces | (+1, 0, 0) | `latomfirst(cell_ind(i+1,ncells(1)), j, k)` |
| | (0, +1, 0) | `latomfirst(i, cell_ind(j+1,ncells(2)), k)` |
| | (0, 0, +1) | `latomfirst(i, j, cell_ind(k+1,ncells(3)))` |
| Edges | (+1, -1, 0) | `latomfirst(cell_ind(i+1,ncells(1)), cell_ind(j-1,ncells(2)), k)` |
| | (+1, 0, -1) | `latomfirst(cell_ind(i+1,ncells(1)), j, cell_ind(k-1,ncells(3)))` |
| | (0, +1, -1) | `latomfirst(i, cell_ind(j+1,ncells(2)), cell_ind(k-1,ncells(3)))` |
| | (0, +1, +1) | `latomfirst(i, cell_ind(j+1,ncells(2)), cell_ind(k+1,ncells(3)))` |
| | (+1, +1, 0) | `latomfirst(cell_ind(i+1,ncells(1)), cell_ind(j+1,ncells(2)), k)` |
| | (+1, 0, +1) | `latomfirst(cell_ind(i+1,ncells(1)), j, cell_ind(k+1,ncells(3)))` |
| Vertices | (+1, -1, -1) | `latomfirst(cell_ind(i+1,ncells(1)), cell_ind(j-1,ncells(2)), cell_ind(k-1,ncells(3)))` |
| | (+1, -1, +1) | `latomfirst(cell_ind(i+1,ncells(1)), cell_ind(j-1,ncells(2)), cell_ind(k+1,ncells(3)))` |
| | (+1, +1, -1) | `latomfirst(cell_ind(i+1,ncells(1)), cell_ind(j+1,ncells(2)), cell_ind(k-1,ncells(3)))` |
| | (+1, +1, +1) | `latomfirst(cell_ind(i+1,ncells(1)), cell_ind(j+1,ncells(2)), cell_ind(k+1,ncells(3)))` |

**Sources:** [src/computef.f90:127-144](), [src/computeg.f90:117-134]()

### Visual Representation of 3x3x3 Stencil

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "3x3x3 Cell Neighborhood"
        direction TB
        CENTER["Central Cell<br/>(i, j, k)"]
        
        subgraph "Forward Half (14 cells checked)"
            SELF["Self<br/>(0,0,0)"]
            F1["(+1,0,0)"]
            F2["(0,+1,0)"]
            F3["(0,0,+1)"]
            E1["(+1,+1,0)"]
            E2["(+1,0,+1)"]
            E3["(0,+1,+1)"]
            E4["(+1,-1,0)"]
            E5["(+1,0,-1)"]
            E6["(0,+1,-1)"]
            V1["(+1,+1,+1)"]
            V2["(+1,+1,-1)"]
            V3["(+1,-1,+1)"]
            V4["(+1,-1,-1)"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Backward Half (13 cells NOT checked)"
            B1["(-1,0,0)"]
            B2["(0,-1,0)"]
            B3["(0,0,-1)"]
            B4["(-1,-1,0)"]
            B5["... 9 more"]
        end
    end
    
    CENTER -.-> SELF
    CENTER -.-> F1
    CENTER -.-> F2
    CENTER -.-> F3
    CENTER -.-> E1
    CENTER -.-> E2
    CENTER -.-> E3
    CENTER -.-> E4
    CENTER -.-> E5
    CENTER -.-> E6
    CENTER -.-> V1
    CENTER -.-> V2
    CENTER -.-> V3
    CENTER -.-> V4
```

The "forward half" ensures each atom pair is evaluated exactly once. Since atom pairs are symmetric (distance from A to B equals distance from B to A), checking only forward neighbors avoids redundant calculations.

**Sources:** [src/computef.f90:127-144](), [src/computeg.f90:117-134]()

### Neighbor Search Implementation

The neighbor search is implemented identically in both `computef.f90` (for objective function evaluation) and `computeg.f90` (for gradient evaluation):

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    START["icell = lcellfirst<br/>Start with first occupied cell"]
    LOOP1{"icell > 0?"}
    CONVERT["call icell_to_cell(icell, ncells, cell)<br/>i = cell(1), j = cell(2), k = cell(3)"]
    ATOM_START["icart = latomfirst(i,j,k)<br/>Get first atom in cell"]
    LOOP2{"icart > 0?"}
    CHECK_TYPE{"comptype(ibtype(icart))?"}
    SEARCH["Call fparc/gparc for:<br/>1. latomnext(icart) [self]<br/>2-4. Face neighbors<br/>5-10. Edge neighbors<br/>11-14. Vertex neighbors"]
    NEXT_ATOM["icart = latomnext(icart)"]
    NEXT_CELL["icell = lcellnext(icell)"]
    END["Complete"]
    
    START --> LOOP1
    LOOP1 -->|"Yes"| CONVERT
    LOOP1 -->|"No"| END
    CONVERT --> ATOM_START
    ATOM_START --> LOOP2
    LOOP2 -->|"Yes"| CHECK_TYPE
    LOOP2 -->|"No"| NEXT_CELL
    CHECK_TYPE -->|"Yes"| SEARCH
    CHECK_TYPE -->|"No"| NEXT_ATOM
    SEARCH --> NEXT_ATOM
    NEXT_ATOM --> LOOP2
    NEXT_CELL --> LOOP1
```

**Implementation in computef.f90:** [src/computef.f90:115-151]()

**Implementation in computeg.f90:** [src/computeg.f90:105-142]()

**Sources:** [src/computef.f90:115-151](), [src/computeg.f90:105-142]()

## Periodic Boundary Conditions

### PBC Module Functions

The `pbc` module provides three key functions for handling periodic boundary conditions:

#### v_in_box: Coordinate Wrapping

```fortran
elemental double precision function v_in_box(v, pbc_min, pbc_length)
   v_in_box = pbc_min + modulo((v - pbc_min), pbc_length)
end function v_in_box
```

Wraps a coordinate into the simulation box: `[pbc_min, pbc_min + pbc_length)`. This is used by `setcell` before computing cell indices.

**Implementation:** [src/pbc.f90:15-18]()

#### delta_vector: Minimum Image Distance

```fortran
elemental double precision function delta_vector(v1, v2, pbc_length)
   delta_vector = v1 - v2
   delta_vector = delta_vector - pbc_length * nint(delta_vector / pbc_length)
end function delta_vector
```

Computes the minimum image convention distance between two coordinates. The result is in the range `(-pbc_length/2, pbc_length/2]`.

**Implementation:** [src/pbc.f90:20-24]()

#### cell_ind: Cell Index Wrapping

```fortran
integer function cell_ind(icell, ncells)
   cell_ind = modulo(icell - 1 + ncells, ncells) + 1
end function cell_ind
```

Wraps cell indices to handle neighbor cells across periodic boundaries (e.g., cell index `ncells+1` wraps to `1`).

**Implementation:** [src/pbc.f90:26-29]()

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:15-29]()

### PBC Configuration Variables

| Variable | Type | Module | Default | Purpose |
|----------|------|--------|---------|---------|
| `using_pbc` | `logical` | `pbc` | `.false.` | Whether PBC are enabled |
| `pbc_min(3)` | `double precision` | `pbc` | - | Minimum box coordinates |
| `pbc_max(3)` | `double precision` | `pbc` | - | Maximum box coordinates |
| `pbc_length(3)` | `double precision` | `pbc` | - | Box dimensions per axis |

These variables are set during input file parsing when the `pbc` keyword is encountered.

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:5-11]()

## Cell Reset Mechanism

The `resetcells` subroutine clears the linked-list structures between optimization iterations. This is necessary because atom positions change, requiring cells to be rebuilt.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    START["resetcells() called"]
    CLEAR["Clear all linked lists:<br/>lcellnext(:) = 0<br/>lcellfirst = 0<br/>latomfirst(:,:,:) = 0<br/>latomnext(:) = 0<br/>empty_cell(:,:,:) = .true."]
    CHECK{"fix == .true.?<br/>(Are there fixed atoms?)"}
    REBUILD["Rebuild cells for fixed atoms:<br/>Loop over fixed atom types<br/>Call setcell for each fixed atom<br/>Add to latomfirst/latomnext<br/>Add to lcellfirst/lcellnext"]
    END["Return"]
    
    START --> CLEAR
    CLEAR --> CHECK
    CHECK -->|"Yes"| REBUILD
    CHECK -->|"No"| END
    REBUILD --> END
```

**Why reset cells?** During optimization, atoms move continuously. Rather than updating the cell lists incrementally (complex and error-prone), Packmol rebuilds them from scratch each iteration. Fixed atoms (if present) are added first so they participate in interactions but don't move.

**Implementation:** [src/resetcells.f90:10-42]()

**Sources:** [src/resetcells.f90:10-42]()

## Integration with Optimization Loop

The spatial management system is invoked during every objective function and gradient evaluation:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant GENCAN as "GENCAN Optimizer"
    participant COMPUTEF as "computef.f90"
    participant COMPUTEG as "computeg.f90"
    participant RESET as "resetcells()"
    participant SETCELL as "setcell()"
    participant FPARC as "fparc()/gparc()"
    
    GENCAN->>COMPUTEF: Evaluate objective f(x)
    COMPUTEF->>RESET: Clear cells
    loop For each atom
        COMPUTEF->>SETCELL: Compute cell indices
        COMPUTEF->>COMPUTEF: Build linked lists
    end
    loop For each occupied cell
        loop For each atom in cell
            COMPUTEF->>FPARC: Evaluate 14-neighbor interactions
        end
    end
    COMPUTEF-->>GENCAN: Return f
    
    GENCAN->>COMPUTEG: Evaluate gradient g(x)
    COMPUTEG->>RESET: Clear cells
    loop For each atom
        COMPUTEG->>SETCELL: Compute cell indices
        COMPUTEG->>COMPUTEG: Build linked lists
    end
    loop For each occupied cell
        loop For each atom in cell
            COMPUTEG->>FPARC: Compute 14-neighbor gradients
        end
    end
    COMPUTEG-->>GENCAN: Return g
```

**Key observations:**
- Cells are rebuilt from scratch on every function/gradient evaluation
- The same 14-cell neighbor pattern is used in both `computef` and `computeg`
- The cell system reduces complexity from O(N²) to O(N) by limiting neighbor checks
- PBC wrapping is applied consistently through `cell_ind` and `delta_vector`

**Sources:** [src/computef.f90:1-154](), [src/computeg.f90:1-246](), [src/resetcells.f90:10-42]()

## Performance Characteristics

### Complexity Analysis

| Operation | Without Cells | With Cells | Scaling Factor |
|-----------|---------------|------------|----------------|
| Pairwise interactions | O(N²) | O(N) | N / (density × cell_size³) |
| Cell assignment | - | O(N) | 1 per atom |
| Neighbor search | - | O(1) per atom | 14 cells maximum |
| Memory overhead | - | O(N + C³) | C = grid dimensions |

The cell system transforms the dominant O(N²) pairwise interaction cost into O(N) by exploiting spatial locality.

### Memory Footprint

| Data Structure | Size | Description |
|----------------|------|-------------|
| `latomfirst` | `ncells(1) × ncells(2) × ncells(3) × 4 bytes` | Cell→atom mapping |
| `latomnext` | `ntotat × 4 bytes` | Atom linked list |
| `lcellfirst` | `4 bytes` | Scalar |
| `lcellnext` | `ncells(1) × ncells(2) × ncells(3) × 4 bytes` | Cell linked list |
| `empty_cell` | `ncells(1) × ncells(2) × ncells(3) × 1 byte` | Occupancy flags |

For a typical system with 10,000 atoms and 20×20×20 cells, the total overhead is approximately:
- `latomfirst`: 8,000 × 4 = 32 KB
- `latomnext`: 10,000 × 4 = 40 KB  
- `lcellnext`: 8,000 × 4 = 32 KB
- `empty_cell`: 8,000 × 1 = 8 KB
- **Total: ~112 KB**

This is negligible compared to the coordinate and gradient storage requirements.

**Sources:** [src/computef.f90:1-154](), [src/computeg.f90:1-246]()

## Module Dependencies

The spatial management system spans multiple modules with clear separation of concerns:

```mermaid
graph TB
    PBC["pbc module<br/>v_in_box, delta_vector, cell_ind"]
    CELL["cell_indexing module<br/>setcell, index_cell, icell_to_cell"]
    DATA["compute_data module<br/>ncells, cell_length, linked lists"]
    RESET["resetcells subroutine<br/>Clear and rebuild cells"]
    COMPUTEF["computef.f90<br/>Use cells for f(x)"]
    COMPUTEG["computeg.f90<br/>Use cells for g(x)"]
    
    PBC --> CELL
    CELL --> COMPUTEF
    CELL --> COMPUTEG
    DATA --> RESET
    DATA --> COMPUTEF
    DATA --> COMPUTEG
    RESET --> COMPUTEF
    RESET --> COMPUTEG
```

**Module locations:**
- `pbc`: [src/pbc.f90:5-32]()
- `cell_indexing`: [src/cell_indexing.f90:1-63]()
- `compute_data`: Referenced in [src/computef.f90:13]()
- `resetcells`: [src/resetcells.f90:10-42]()

**Sources:** [src/pbc.f90:5-32](), [src/cell_indexing.f90:1-63](), [src/computef.f90:1-154](), [src/computeg.f90:1-246](), [src/resetcells.f90:10-42]()
